title: Towards practical and efficient home‑based facial geometry and appearance capture with consistent topology
abstractText: Abstract Facial geometry and appearance capture are a foundational technique for digital human creation in the metaverse. Existing methods either rely on expensive hardware or suffer from low efficiency and inconsistent topology. This paper proposes a practical, low-cost, and fully automatic system for high-quality facial asset reconstruction from smartphone videos. The method adopts a sequential pipeline: multi-view stereo reconstructs detailed geometry, followed by non-rigid ICP template fitting to ensure topology consistency. A 2D multi-resolution hash grid in UV space is used to model reflectance, avoiding texture bleeding and hyperparameter tuning. Experiments show that the method reconstructs relightable facial assets in 8 minutes while maintaining quality comparable to state-of-the-art approaches. This work advances accessible and production-ready facial capture for everyday users. Code is available here .

title: An Image Is Worth K Topics: A Visual Structural Topic Model with Pretrained Image Embeddings
abstractText: Abstract Political scientists are increasingly interested in analyzing visual content at scale. However, the existing computational toolbox is still in need of methods and models attuned to the specific challenges and goals of social and political inquiry. In this article, we introduce a visual structural topic model (vSTM) that combines continuous image embeddings with a structural topic model. This has important advantages compared to existing approaches. First, continuous embeddings allow the model to capture the semantic complexity of images, which is relevant to the study of politics. A consequence of using continuous embeddings is that we can directly use off-the-shelf pretrained deep learning models, offering state-of-the-art performance in image analysis tasks while saving time, cost and resources. Second, the structural topic model provides the ability to analyze how topics and covariates are related, while maintaining a nuanced representation of images as a mixture of multiple topics. In our experiments, we show that the vSTM is able to identify topics that are interpretable, coherent and relevant to the study of online political communication.

title: Systematic Improvement of Trial States in Phaseless Auxiliary-Field Quantum Monte Carlo
abstractText: Abstract We extend the use of coupled cluster (CC) trial states in the phaseless auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (AFQMC) method beyond single and double excitations to include both triple and quadruple excitations. With this AFQMC/CC hierarchy, we are able to systematically benchmark the method’s performance on molecular systems as the quality of the trial is improved. Our results show that the phaseless AFQMC energy improves systematically and is typically significantly more accurate than the energy of the underlying trial state. However, the relative improvement compared to the trial CC energy decreases as we ascend the CC hierarchy. As the CC wave function is usually further approximated when used as an AFQMC trial, we also explore the relationship between the components of the CC wave function and the resulting AFQMC/CC error. Our results suggest that improving the representation of the CC wave function in the AFQMC trial does not always lower the bias even when it increases the fidelity of the trial with the exact ground state.

title: Long-range spectral entanglement and quantum correlations in highly nondegenerate multi-comb and ultrafast systems
abstractText: Abstract Frequency combs are multimode photonic systems that underlie countless precision sensing and metrology applications. Since their invention over two decades ago, numerous efforts have pushed frequency combs to broader bandwidths and more stable operation. More recently, quantum squeezing and entanglement have been explored in single-comb systems for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum-enhanced spectroscopy. However, the production of bright quantum light across multiple nondegenerate pulses or frequency combs, a key technology for multispectral applications, remains largely unexplored. In this work, we explore a mechanism that generates a series of nonlinearly coupled bright frequency combs through cascaded three-wave upconversion and downconversion processes mediated by a single idler comb. We consider both discrete combs and broadband ultrafast pulse systems, showing how these systems generate inter- and intracomb two-mode squeezing and entanglement directly in the frequency basis, spanning a large spectral range. Furthermore, we demonstrate how these systems can be engineered to produce target cluster states and concentrated two-mode squeezing through covariance matrix optimization. Our findings uncover a new multimode quantum regime enabled by hierarchical nonlinear interactions in two frequency dimensions, unlocking applications such as entanglement-assisted spectroscopy, squeezing-enhanced pump-probe measurements, quantum spectral multiplexing, and spectrally addressable cluster state generation for quantum information science.

title: Artificial intelligence applications relevant to infective endocarditis in an oral–systemic context: a scoping review
abstractText: This project explores the applications of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the prevention, early detection, diagnosis, and management of Infective Endocarditis (IE), particularly in cases originating from oral or dental infections. Infective Endocarditis remains a life-threatening disease often linked to oral microorganisms entering the bloodstream through dental infections or procedures. Despite this significant association, the integration of AI in studying and managing oral-origin IE has not been systematically mapped. This scoping review aims to identify, categorize, and synthesize existing evidence on how AI and machine learning models have been used to improve diagnostic accuracy, risk prediction, and clinical decision-making in IE. It will also highlight methodological trends, research gaps, and opportunities for future interdisciplinary collaboration among dentistry, cardiology, microbiology, and data science. The expected outcome of this project is to provide a comprehensive overview of current research efforts, summarize AI model performance in IE-related studies, and propose directions for future work that may enhance early detection and prevention strategies linking oral health and cardiovascular disease.

title: Pediatric emergency medicine providers’ experience with digital sexual exposure and abuse
abstractText: BACKGROUND Digital devices and online platforms are a ubiquitous part of childhood and adolescence, and offer both opportunities and risks. One of those risks is digital sexual exposure and abuse, which emerging research finds to be highly prevalent. Pediatric Emergency Medicine (PEM) providers are first responders, mandated reporters and trusted professionals, but how knowledgeable and prepared they are to address these issues is their practice is unknown. OBJECTIVE To assess the familiarity, experiences, and concerns of PEM providers in the U.S with identifying and supporting victims of digital sexual abuse in their clinical practice. METHODS PEM providers (n=286), recruited through a PEM listserv, were surveyed anonymously about how often patients and/or their parents shared concerns about digitally-mediated sexual content or abuse, to what extent presentations of suicidal ideation/attempts were related to digitally-mediated sexual abuse, provider familiarity with different types of digital sexual content and abuse, what resources providers used to support patients, and what additional information or supports they felt were needed to address these topics in their clinical practice. RESULTS Though respondents were familiar with some terms (e.g., sexting, cyberbullying related to sexual images), less than 1 in 5 respondents reported feeling prepared to address sextortion, cyberflashing, or porn addiction. More than 20% of providers reported seeing digital-mediated sexual abuse in their clinical practice monthly or more often, though many reported not asking or screening for these types of abuse. Almost 2/3 of respondents had had patients with suicidal ideation or attempt that was associated with non-consensual image sharing and/or cyberbullying around sexual images. Providers used hospital social work and psychological services to support patients but wanted more education on screening and treating, more resources for families, and greater support from K-12 settings for families. CONCLUSIONS Though based on a convenience sample drawn from the largest PEM listserv, findings indicate the need for more educational resources, updated screening tools, reporting mechanisms, and family-accessible resources for addressing digitally-mediated sexual exposure and abuse among pediatric patients.

EFFICACY AND SAFETY OF RITUXIMAB PLUS DOSE ADJUSTED ETOPOSIDE, PREDNISONE, VINCRISTINE, CYCLOPHOSPHAMIDE AND DOXORUBICIN (R-DA-EPOCH) REGIMEN IN HIGH GRADE DIFFUSE LARGE B- CELL LYMPHOMA PATIENTS (HG-DLBCL)
abstractText: Objective: To determine the efficacy and safety of rituximab plus dose-adjusted etoposide, prednisone, vincristine, cyclophosphamide and doxorubicin (R-DA-EPOCH) regimen in patients with high-grade diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (HG-DLBCL). Study Design: Descriptive case series. Methodology: A This study was coducted at the Department of Medical Oncology, INMOL Hospital, Lahore. A total of 87 patients aged 18–60 years diagnosed with HG-DLBCL were included through non-probability consecutive sampling. All patients received six cycles of R-DA-EPOCH every three weeks, followed by FDG-PET/CT evaluation four weeks after treatment completion. Results: The mean age of patients was 48.6 ± 9.3 years, with 57.5% males. Complete response was achieved in 65.5% of patients, and partial response in 18.4%, yielding an overall response rate of 83.9%. Non-response and disease progression were observed in 9.2% and 6.9% of patients, respectively. Hematologic toxicities such as neutropenia, anemia, and thrombocytopenia were common but manageable. No treatment-related mortality occurred, and 93.1% of patients completed all chemotherapy cycles. Conclusion: It is concluded that the R-DA-EPOCH regimen is an effective and well-tolerated treatment option for high-grade DLBCL, achieving high response rates with acceptable toxicity.

title: TO STUDY THE RESPONSE RATE OF HYPO-FRACTIONATED BLADDER PRESERVATION RADIOTHERAPY IN MUSCLE INVASIVE BLADDER CANCER
abstractText: Objective: To determine the response rate of hypofractionated bladder-preservation radiotherapy in patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer according to RECIST criteria. Study Design: Descriptive case series. Place and Duration of Study: Department of Radiotherapy, Institute of Nuclear Medicine & Oncology (INMOL), Lahore, from June 2025 to September 2025. Methodology: A total of 66 patients aged 25–70 years with histopathologically confirmed muscle-invasive bladder cancer (T2–T4a, N0–N1, M0) and ECOG performance status 0–1 were enrolled using non-probability consecutive sampling. Results: The mean age of patients was 49.8 ± 11.6 years, and 78.8% were males. Complete response was observed in 74.2% of patients, partial response in 13.6%, stable disease in 7.6%, and progressive disease in 4.6%, yielding an overall response rate of 87.8%. Response rates were highest in T2-stage tumors and declined with advancing tumor stage. Grade III toxicity occurred infrequently, and treatment interruption was required in only 3.0% of patients. Conclusion: Hypofractionated bladder-preservation radiotherapy achieves a high response rate with acceptable acute toxicity in muscle-invasive bladder cancer, representing an effective and well-tolerated bladder-sparing treatment option for appropriately selected patients.

What is compassion connected to, and does it differ by gender and age? A network analysis of compassion, self-compassion, mindfulness, empathy and mental health
abstractText: Abstract Compassion is an emotional state experienced in response to witnessing the suffering of others, accompanied by an internal motivation to help. When directed toward the self, it is referred to as self-compassion. Previous research suggests that compassion and self-compassion are closely related to mindfulness and empathy, contributing to reductions in anxiety and depression and to the enhancement of positive affect. Accordingly, this study employed network analysis to explore the complex structure of interactions among these psychological variables. A total of 1,020 Korean adults completed measures of compassion, self-compassion, mindfulness, empathy, well-being, and negative affect (depression, anxiety, and stress). An EBICglasso network was estimated in R (version 4.5.1). Centrality indices were computed, and subgroup networks were constructed by gender and age to compare structural differences. The results showed that compassion was closely connected to empathy, whereas self-compassion was more strongly linked to mindfulness and well-being; the capacities to feel, tolerate, and alleviate suffering emerged as central nodes. In the gender-based networks, compassion and self-compassion among men tended to be organized primarily around cognitive factors, whereas women exhibited a pattern in which the behavioral motivation for compassion was activated relatively immediately, even in the absence of emotional responding. In the age-based networks, the influence of suffering tolerance was most pronounced in middle-aged adults, while the role of empathy diminished and the role of mindfulness expanded in older adults. By examining compassion at the level of its constituent elements and visualizing the interaction structure among related variables, this study provides an empirical foundation for extending theoretical understanding and for developing tailored intervention strategies.

title: Characterizing the spatiotemporal variability in methane emissions from a large municipal solid waste landfill in Québec, Canada
abstractText: Landfills contributed 18% of anthropogenic methane (CH4) emissions in Canada in 2023. Regulatory efforts have been implemented to reduce these emissions by 50% by 2030 relative to 2019 levels. A comprehensive understanding of the spatiotemporal variability of landfill CH4 emissions is required to support the effective implementation of these policies. In this study, we investigated the spatiotemporal variability of CH4 emissions at a large municipal solid waste landfill in Sainte-Sophie, Québec, Canada, from May to July 2022. We used four measurement methods covering different spatial scales from point to facility levels: static chambers (point scale), eddy covariance and semiconductor sensors (landfill section scale), and mobile concentration surveys (facility scale). Multi-scale measurements identified CH4 emission hotspots in the active section and intermediate cover area, as well as near the leachate treatment facility in the landfill. At the facility scale, an average emission rate of 14,000 ± 5,100 kg day-1 from the entire landfill was estimated using a backward Lagrangian stochastic model. At the section and point scales, we characterized spatiotemporal CH4 emission patterns and identified several CH4 emission hotspots and key drivers. No pronounced temporal patterns of CH4 emissions were observed over the two-month study period. The findings highlight that identifying key emission hotspots at the facility scale, followed by continued monitoring at finer spatial scales, is essential for effectively characterizing CH­4 emissions. Such efforts can support the effective implementation of the regulatory frameworks aimed at mitigating CH4 emissions from landfills.

title: Antibiotic prescribing patterns among outpatients using the who aware classification in health facilities in Tete and Sofala, Mozambique: a cross-sectional study
abstractText: Abstract Background Antibiotic overuse is a major driver of antimicrobial resistance (AMR), a global public health concern, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa where a high burden of infectious diseases and predominantly empirical diagnosis contribute to inappropriate use. The World Health Organization (WHO) AWaRe (Access, Watch, Reserve) classification supports rational prescribing by enabling the monitoring of antibiotic use patterns. However, data on AWaRe-based antibiotic use in Mozambique, especially in outpatient settings, remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate antibiotic prescribing patterns among outpatients using the WHO AWaRe classification in health facilities in Tete and Sofala, Mozambique. Methods Secondary data from outpatient prescriptions at two health facilities in Mozambique, Health Center No. 3 in Tete Province and Caia District Hospital in Sofala Province, were analyzed. Patients of all ages attended between November 2025 and January 2026 with at least one antibiotic prescribed were included (n = 387). Antibiotic prescribing patterns were evaluated using the WHO AWaRe classification and WHO/INRUD prescribing indicators. Results Among the 387 prescriptions included, a total of 435 antibiotics were prescribed. Most patients received one antibiotic (89.4%), while 6.7% received two and 3.9% received three or more. Cotrimoxazole was the most frequently prescribed antibiotic (42.8%), followed by amoxicillin (20.2%) and metronidazole (11.3%). According to the AWaRe classification, 85.7% of antibiotics belonged to the Access group and 12.4% to the Watch group, with no prescriptions from the Reserve group. All antibiotics were prescribed by their generic names and were included in the essential medicines list. Total antibiotic consumption was 121.91 DDD/1,000 inhabitants/day, with amoxicillin (50.22) and ciprofloxacin (23.59) showing the highest utilization rates. Conclusion Antibiotic prescribing among outpatients in this study met the WHO target for the Access group, indicating overall alignment with recommended practices. However, the use of Watch antibiotics, particularly macrolides, highlights the need to strengthen antimicrobial stewardship efforts to ensure more rational use. The implementation of WHO recommendations, including the AWaRe classification, together with improved adherence to clinical guidelines and targeted training of healthcare providers, is essential to optimize prescribing practices in outpatient settings.

title: ICUBE5: A Conceptual Multidimensional Benchmarking Framework for AI-Native Secure 6G Edge Architectures
abstractText: The trend towards sixth-generation (6G) networks requires a new network architecture capable of incorporating artificial intelligence (AI), distributed edge intelligence, security, governance, adaptability, and sustainability into increasingly heterogeneous computing and communication environments. Present methods to achieve such network architectures address only the optimisation, security, governance, or energy-efficiency issues separately, making it difficult to assess the maturity of a particular architecture across all of these dimensions. This paper proposes an AI-native secure edge architecture and introduces ICUBE5, a conceptual multidimensional benchmarking framework for assessing AI-enabled 6G edge architectures across five dimensions: AI Maturity, Security Resilience, Governance Alignment, Adaptive Stability, and Sustainability Efficiency. The framework provides a structured approach for normalising dimension-specific indicators and combining them through configurable weighting schemes that can be adapted to deployment priorities. Illustrative weighting scenarios are presented for general-purpose, industrial automation, smart-city, and energy-constrained edge environments to demonstrate how contextual priorities can influence the composite ICUBE5 score. A comparative analytical illustration involving cloud-centric, edge-centric, and AI-native secure edge architectural archetypes further demonstrates the application of the framework. Under the illustrative assumptions used in the analysis, the proposed AI-native secure edge architecture produces the highest composite ICUBE5 score, while the results remain conceptual rather than empirical measurements of deployed systems. The framework also incorporates security and governance considerations associated with adversarial machine learning, federated learning, trustworthy AI, and emerging regulatory requirements. ICUBE5 is therefore positioned as a benchmarking construct rather than a validated performance index. Future research will validate the framework through simulation and experimental testbeds, using measurable network, security, governance, adaptive-control, and energy-efficiency indicators. The proposed framework provides a basis for structured comparison and context-sensitive evaluation of emerging AI-native 6G edge architectures.

title: Regional heterogeneity in the association between antiretroviral therapy coverage and HIV epidemiology in Sub-Saharan Africa: a longitudinal ecological study of 38 countries (2010–2022)
abstractText: Abstract Introduction : Antiretroviral therapy (ART) coverage has expanded rapidly in sub-Saharan Africa, but the population-level impact on HIV incidence, mortality and prevalence across different sub-regions remains uncertain. We quantified the association between ART coverage and these epidemiological indicators from 2010 to 2022. Methods : We conducted a longitudinal ecological study using country-level data from 38 sub-Saharan African countries (494 observations) from UNAIDS, the World Bank and the UNDP. Fixed-effects panel regression models with log-transformed variables estimated elasticities: β represents the percentage change in the outcome per 1% change in ART coverage. Results are presented per 10% ART increase for interpretability. Regional interaction terms (East Africa as reference) tested effect heterogeneity, with real effects in other regions calculated as β_ART + β_interaction. Bootstrapping generated 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for overall percentage changes. Results : Regional ART coverage increased from 22% to 75% between 2010 and 2022. Overall, HIV incidence fell by 65% (95% CI 60–70), mortality by 72% (68–76), and prevalence by 33% (30–36). Regarding incidence, a 10% increase in ART coverage was associated with a 1.6% reduction in East Africa (β_ART = − 0.16, 95% CI − 0.24 to − 0.08); the effect was significantly attenuated in West Africa (real β = − 0.02, 0.2% reduction; interaction p = 0.003) but similar in Central and Southern Africa (interaction p > 0.05). For mortality, a 10% ART increase was associated with a 4.2% reduction in East Africa (β_ART = − 0.42, 95% CI − 0.49 to − 0.35); significant attenuation was observed elsewhere, with real effects of − 0.26 (2.6% reduction) in West Africa, − 0.21 (2.1%) in Southern Africa, and − 0.32 (3.2%) in Central Africa (all interaction p < 0.05). For prevalence, a 10% ART increase was associated with a 1.0% reduction in East Africa (β_ART = − 0.10, 95% CI − 0.13 to − 0.07); the effect was similar in West Africa (interaction p = 0.60) but significantly attenuated in Central and Southern Africa (real β = − 0.04, 0.4% reduction; interaction p < 0.01), and the association was strongly modified by the incidence–mortality ratio (interaction β = 0.29, p < 0.001). Had ART coverage remained at 2010 levels, an estimated 1.2 million (95% CI 1.0–1.4) additional deaths would have occurred. Conclusion : ART scale-up substantially reduced HIV incidence and mortality across all sub-Saharan African regions, with significant though attenuated effects in West, Southern and Central Africa. Prevalence is an unreliable standalone indicator of ART programme success. Regional tailoring of ART strategies and continued health system investments remain essential.

title: Range-based finishing enhances omega-3 fatty acids and forage-derived metabolites in bison meat across a seven-treatment comparison
abstractText: Abstract Background Finishing practices influence the biochemical composition of bison ( Bison bison ) meat, with potential implications for animal health and human nutrition. This study evaluated seven representative finishing systems spanning a range of extensive and intensive production systems, with additional contrasts in forage diversity, corn supplementation, and stocking density to determine their effects on the fatty acid and phytonutrient profiles of bison striploins ( M. longissimus lumborum ). Treatments included range-finished bison grazing either diverse native pastures (~200 plant species) or lower-diversity pastures (~90 plant species), with or without corn supplementation, as well as pen-finished bison managed under varying feed formulations and stocking densities, including a conventional total mixed ration (TMR) group. Fatty acids were analyzed by gas chromatography–flame ionization detection (GC-FID), and targeted metabolomic profiling of phytonutrient-derived metabolites was performed using liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (LC–MS/MS). Results Range-finished bison exhibited higher concentrations of alpha-linolenic acid (ALA; C18:3n-3; P < 0.0001), docosapentaenoic acid (DPA; C22:5n-3; P < 0.0001), and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA; C22:6n-3; P < 0.0001), and lower n-6:n-3 ratios (2.8–3.6) than pen-finished bison (5.0–7.3; P < 0.0001). Metabolomic profiling revealed enrichment of hippuric acid, catechol, and shikimic acid (candidate biomarkers associated with forage intake and polyphenolic metabolism) in range-finished systems, whereas 3-(4-hydroxyphenyl)lactic acid, a potential grain-associated metabolite, was higher in pen-finished bison than in the unsupplemented range-finished systems (all P < 0.05). Conclusions Range-finished systems enhanced omega-3 fatty acid and phytonutrient-related metabolite profiles, whereas the conventional TMR feedlot treatment yielded the lowest levels and the free-choice corn-and-hay pen system yielded an intermediate profile. Overall, the clearest nutritional contrast was between range-finished and pen-finished systems, whereas differences attributable to forage diversity or stocking density were comparatively modest. These findings indicate that finishing system strongly influences the biochemical composition of bison meat, although comparisons involving the conventional TMR feedlot treatment should be interpreted cautiously because that group originated from a separate breeding herd.

title: Mid-IR diffraction gratings fabricated via nanoimprint lithography for chirped pulse amplification
abstractText: Abstract Lasers emitting in the 2 µm spectral region have attracted considerable attention in recent years owing to their wide-ranging applications in science and industry, including the detection of atmospheric constituents like H 2 O, surgical procedures in medicine, and LIDAR technologies. In industry, they can be utilized in high-precision machining and materials engineering. For these latter purposes, a high-power laser is needed. This can be achieved by amplifying the laser pulse, typically using chirped pulse amplification (CPA). The crucial component of CPA, used for the compression and stretching steps, is the grating waveguide structure (GWS). In the present paper, we explore the fabrication of GWSs via nanoimprint lithography (NIL) for operation at a central wavelength of 2050 nm. The GWSs were integrated into the topmost hafnium oxide (HfO₂) layer of a multilayer HfO₂/SiO₂ dielectric mirror. The fabrication process comprised master wafer production via laser interference lithography, stamp fabrication, NIL patterning, and reactive-ion etching. The desired etch depth in HfO 2 was a key challenge, which was addressed by implementing a chromium hard mask and a Taguchi experimental design. Scanning electron microscopy and atomic force microscopy revealed slight deviations from the designed GWS dimensions, mainly in the duty cycle. Consequently, the maximum diffraction efficiency was slightly blue-shifted and measured to be 97% at 2030 nm, i.e., lower than the 99% predicted theoretically. Our study demonstrates the feasibility of using NIL for large-area GWS fabrication with high diffraction efficiency.

title: Thermal behavior and microstructure control of Ti6Al4V alloy in laser directed energy deposition using synchronous gas cooling strategy
abstractText: Synchronous gas cooling-assisted laser directed energy deposition is a novel method for the in-situ active regulation of the microstructure of Ti6Al4V alloy. This study systematically investigates the influence of different gas cooling flow rates on the grain evolution and phase structure characteristics of Ti6Al4V alloy fabricated by laser directed energy deposition, and reveals the thermal behavior mechanism through numerical simulation. The results show that, with increasing gas cooling flow rate, the α′ phase gradually transforms from an acicular morphology to a lath-like morphology, accompanied by a significant reduction in aspect ratio and a substantial improvement in size uniformity. Regarding β grain evolution, increasing the gas cooling flow rate suppresses the transition from columnar grains to equiaxed grains, promotes columnar grain growth, significantly reduces texture intensity, and increases dislocation density. However, the β grain size exhibits a trend of first decreasing and then increasing. Temperature-field analysis indicates that the cold jet induces a pronounced heat-sink effect through forced convective heat transfer, forming a distinctive temperature field characterized by lower temperatures in the cold-jet action zone and higher temperatures on both sides. Increasing the gas cooling flow rate not only reduces the peak temperature of the molten pool, but also increases the temperature gradient and cooling rate at the solidification interface, effectively narrowing the heat-affected zone and phase-transformation zone, while improving the temperature-field uniformity behind the center of the cold jet.

title: Planning operational costs and CO2 emissions of municipal solid waste collection: A case study in Italy
abstractText: Waste collection represents the major component of municipal solid waste management costs and a direct source of greenhouse gas emissions. Environmental assessments often rely on generic transport emission factors that do not adequately reflect the real operating conditions of collection vehicles. To address this gap, a field monitoring campaign was carried out in central Tuscany (Italy), involving 233 collection routes operated under different collection systems, vehicle types and fuels. Measured fuel consumption data were used to estimate collection-phase CO₂ emissions and to develop a modelling framework able to predict operational costs and CO₂ emissions as a function of linear population density (LPD) and per capita waste generation.Monitoring results showed that energy consumption and CO₂ emissions during collection were systematically higher than values reported in standard transport inventories, particularly for heavy-duty vehicles. Modelling results revealed an inverse relationship between LPD and both costs and CO₂ emissions per tonne of collected waste, highlighting the importance of local context in collection planning.From an environmental perspective, the street-bin system became more carbon-efficient above 75 inhabitants·km⁻¹, although differences compared with the door-to-door system remained relatively limited. From an economic perspective, the street-bin system was the most cost-effective option across most density ranges, while the door-to-door system was competitive only in very low-density contexts.The findings demonstrate the importance of using empirically derived emission factors and accounting for territorial characteristics when evaluating and planning waste collection services. The proposed framework provides a transferable tool to support context-sensitive planning of municipal solid waste collection systems.

Measuring what future physicians know about contraception: development and validation of the clinical contraceptive knowledge test (CCKT) in Vietnam using item response theory
abstractText: Abstract Background Accurate measurement of contraceptive knowledge among medical students remains a critical challenge due to limitations of traditional assessment tools. This study aimed to develop and validate the Clinical Contraceptive Knowledge Test (CCKT) using a modern psychometric framework. Methods A cross-sectional multicenter study was conducted among undergraduate medical students in Vietnam (723 recruited; 636 retained for analysis). The instrument was developed through four sequential phases: (1) Item generation based on Bloom’s taxonomy and WHO Medical Eligibility Criteria (MEC), (2) expert review for content validity, (3) pilot testing using Classical Test Theory, and (4) large-scale validation using Item Response Theory. A two-parameter logistic (2PL) IRT model was applied to evaluate item characteristics, dimensionality, and measurement precision. Results The final instrument, CCKT-18, demonstrated strong psychometric performance. A unidimensional 2PL model was retained based on comparable fit to multidimensional models and high inter-factor correlations (r > 0.80). Model fit indices indicated good fit (CFI = 0.983, TLI = 0.980, RMSEA = 0.036, SRMR = 0.039). The scale showed high measurement precision across a broad range of ability levels, with peak information around the average proficiency level (marginal reliability = 0.844). Item parameters were stable in sensitivity analyses (ΔCFI = 0.003), supporting model robustness. DIF analyses supported measurement invariance across sex, although several items demonstrated DIF across the training stage. Conclusion The CCKT-18 is a valid, reliable, and robust instrument for assessing contraceptive knowledge among medical students. Its IRT-based framework enables precise, competency-oriented evaluation and provides actionable insights for targeted curriculum improvement in reproductive health education.

title: Back-localized restlessness without limb involvement: a case with features suggestive of the restless legs syndrome spectrum
abstractText: Abstract Background Restless legs syndrome (RLS) is typically characterized by unpleasant sensations in the lower limbs and an urge to move the legs. Abnormal sensations localized to the back without limb involvement have been reported as restless back syndrome; however, such presentations do not necessarily fulfill the diagnostic criteria for typical RLS, and their classification requires cautious interpretation. Although associations between RLS and autonomic symptoms, including urinary symptoms, have been reported, the clinical significance of cases in which urinary urgency and generalized heat sensation occur synchronously with back-localized abnormal sensations remains unclear. Case presentation A 50-year-old man presented with a restless and uncomfortable sensation localized to the interscapular region. The symptoms occurred while lying at rest after going to bed, before sleep onset, were accompanied by an urge to move the back or body, and were temporarily relieved by movement. However, he had no urge to move the legs and no limb symptoms. When the symptoms occurred, urinary urgency and generalized heat sensation appeared during the same time period. During ropinirole use, these symptoms were suppressed based on the patient’s report. Subsequently, during acupressure mat use, the back symptoms occurred rarely or not at all, whereas urinary urgency and generalized heat sensation partially persisted. The assessment was based on an online medical history interview and patient-provided materials. Conclusions Although this case cannot be diagnosed as typical RLS, its clinical course may be cautiously interpreted as possible restless back syndrome within the RLS spectrum. The synchronous occurrence of urinary urgency and generalized heat sensation with the back symptoms, as well as the patient-reported improvement of the back symptoms during acupressure mat use, is noteworthy; however, neither finding demonstrates a pathophysiological association or treatment efficacy based on this single case.

title: Association of imipenem/cilastatin with development of acute kidney injury in critically ill patients requiring carbapenem treatment
abstractText: Abstract Cilastatin is an inhibitor of drug metabolism in the kidney which is only available for human use in combination with imipenem, a carbapenem antibiotic, as imipenem/cilastatin (I/C). Animal studies demonstrate cilastatin protects against acute kidney injury (AKI) and clinical studies suggest I/C may reduce the risk of AKI. However, the effective dose of cilastatin in animal studies is higher than that approved with imipenem, and rigorous assessment of the effect of I/C on AKI in patients with high risk of AKI, such as those in the intensive care unit (ICU), is indicated. To address this issue, we conducted a retrospective cohort study using 3 large ICU databases, including Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care III (MIMIC-III), MIMIC-IV, and the Amsterdam University Medical Center database (AUMC). Total 3916 patients were included and patients treated with I/C or non-cilastatin carbapenems (NCC) were compared using propensity score-based overlap weighting analysis. AKI development or progression was less commonly observed in I/C-treated patients than in NCC-treated patients in MIMIC-III (odds ratio [OR] and 95% confidence interval of I/C group: 0.51 [0.30–0.85]) while the outcome was similar between the groups in MIMIC-IV (OR: 1.22 [0.80–1.86]) and in AUMC (OR: 1.07 [0.77–1.48]). The outcome development was also similar between the groups with the overall analysis across all datasets by random effect model meta-analysis (OR: 0.89 [0.54–1.48]). In conclusion, I/C and other carbapenems do not differentially associate with AKI risks in ICU, and its putative effects may depend on patient characteristics and clinical settings.

title: Does the direct anterior learning curve persist after fellowship training? A single-center comparative cohort study
abstractText: Abstract Introduction : The direct-anterior-approach (DAA) for total hip arthroplasty (THA) has significant benefits but has historically been associated with a steep learning curve. However, modern training in the approach may eliminate that learning curve. We hypothesize that newly graduated surgeons with specific training in the DAA would show no difference in complication rates compared to senior DAA surgeons. Methods : This retrospective cohort study included 600 primary THAs performed via a DAA from a single institution between November 2019 and February 2025 with a minimum of 90-day follow up. Intra- and post-operative complications were compared between the following two groups: the first 100 cases of each of three junior fellowship-trained arthroplasty surgeons (“Junior”) and the most recent 300 cases of a senior fellowship-trained arthroplasty surgeon (“Senior”). Results: The incidence of operative complications was low and showed no significant difference between groups (Junior − 30 (10.0%) vs Senior − 23 (7.7%), p = 0.39). Subgroup analyses showed no between-group differences for DVT (1.3 vs 0.7%, p = 0.686), PE (0.7 vs 0.3%, p = 1.000), hematoma (0.3 vs 1.0%, p = 0.62), dislocation (1.3 vs 0.3%, p = 0.37), periprosthetic fracture (1.7 vs 1.0%, p = 0.73), neuropraxia (1.3 vs 2.0%, p = 0.75), prosthetic joint infection (1.0 vs 0.3%, p = 0.62), or wound complications (2.3 vs 2.3%, p = 1.00) (Table 2). Medical events were infrequent, with a non-significant trend toward more events in the Senior cohort (Junior − 7 (2.3%) vs Senior − 14 (4.7%), p = 0.181). Operative time was found to be longer among Junior surgeons (92.3 vs 68.5 minutes, p < 0.0001). No difference in patient reported outcome measures (PROMs) were found at 90 day follow up between junior and senior surgeon cohorts. Conclusion : The results of this study suggest that while fellowship-trained DAA surgeons starting practice have longer operative times, there is no difference in overall complication rates or patient-reported functional outcomes when compared to a Senior DAA surgeon. This demonstrates that the historical learning curve surrounding adoption of the DAA may not apply with exposure to the approach during adult-reconstruction fellowship training.

title: Agar oligosaccharides mitigate lipopolysaccharide-induced apoptosis and inflammatory damage in rumen epithelial cells via the TLR4–MyD88–NF-B signaling pathway
abstractText: Abstract Agar oligosaccharide (AOS) is an oligosaccharide with a degree of polymerization (DP) of agarose, which is degraded by hydrolysis, chemical degradation, and other methods, and has an oligosaccharide with a DP of less than 20. It has anti-inflammatory and anti-apoptotic effects, but its intervention effect and mechanism on rumen epithelial damage are still unclear. Therefore, this study intends to study and analyze the regulatory effect of AOS on LPS-induced rumen epithelial cell damage in sheep through in vitro LPS-induced rumen epithelial cell injury model, so as to provide a reference idea for AOS as a green feed additive to alleviate ruminant Subacute rumen acidosis (SARA) or other metabolic diseases. First, the ovine rumen epithelial cells were divided into a control group and four AOS concentration groups (1, 15, 50, 100 μg/mL), and three independent biological replicates were set up in each group to stimulate the cells for 6, 12, 18, and 24 h respectively to determine the optimal AOS treatment time and concentration. The results showed that the content of pro-inflammatory cytokines and the relative expression of pro-apoptotic genes in rumen epithelial cells cultured with 15 µg/mL AOS for 18 h were significantly reduced (p<0.05), and the relative expression of cell viability and inhibition of apoptosis genes were significantly increased (p<0.05), and there were no adverse effects on the cells under the intervention of the concentration of this treatment and the time of the treatment. Second, establish a cell injury model. The cells were divided into a control group and four Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) concentration groups (1, 15, 50, 100 µg/mL), with three independent biological replicates in each group, and the cells were stimulated for 6, 12, and 24 hours. The results showed that after culturing rumen epithelial cells with 50 µg/mL LPS for 24 hours, reactive oxygen species (ROS), pro-inflammatory cytokine levels, and the relative expression of pro-apoptotic genes were significantly increased (p<0.05), while cell viability and the relative expression of anti-apoptotic genes were significantly decreased (p<0.05). Therefore, this condition was determined as the injury model. Third, based on the above experimental results, the cells were divided into a control group (CON group), LPS group, and AOS+LPS group (A+L group) to further explore the effect of AOS on LPS-induced rumen epithelial cell injury. The results showed that 50 µg/mL LPS incubation for 24 h could cause suitable damage to the cells. Cell morphology was improved and cell viability was significantly higher in the A+L group (p<0.05). The A+L group significantly decreased the reactive oxygen species (ROS) fluorescence intensity and interleukin-6 (IL-6) , IL-8, IL-1β and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) contents and increased the immunoglobulin A (IgA) , IgM, and IgG contents (p<0.05). The apoptosis rate were significantly reduced (p<0.05). In addition, the A+L group significantly inhibited the expression of genes and proteins related to the Toll-like Receptor 4-Myeloid Differentiationfactor 88-Nuclear Factor-κB (TLR4-MyD88-NF-κB) signaling pathway. In summary, AOS attenuated LPS-induced apoptosis and inflammatory injury in rumen epithelial cells in vitro via the TLR4-MyD88-NF-κB signaling pathway.

title: PGK1 expression varies across breast cancer molecular subtypes and is associated with overall survival in the TCGA BRCA cohort
abstractText: Abstract Purpose Phosphoglycerate kinase 1 (PGK1) is a glycolytic enzyme implicated in cancer metabolism and breast cancer progression, but reported survival associations may be confounded by molecular subtype and stage. Methods We analyzed official TCGA-BRCA PanCancer Atlas RNA-seq V2 RSEM and clinical files from the cBioPortal DataHub. PGK1 expression was evaluated in 1,082 primary tumors, including 981 with PAM50 annotation. Overall-survival analyses included 915 patients in the four principal PAM50 subtypes with complete age, AJCC stage, survival, and expression data (118 deaths). PGK1 was modeled as a standardized continuous variable. The primary Cox model adjusted for age and stratified the baseline hazard by stage and PAM50 subtype. Co-expression was assessed in a curated 119-gene panel using prespecified mean z-score composite signatures. Results PGK1 expression differed across PAM50 subtypes (P = 4.35×10⁻⁵⁷) and was highest in HER2-enriched tumors. Higher PGK1 was associated with shorter overall survival in univariate analysis (hazard ratio [HR] per 1-SD increase, 1.55; 95% CI, 1.31–1.85; P = 7.10×10⁻⁷) and in the primary stratified model (HR, 1.41; 95% CI, 1.13–1.76; P = 0.002). PGK1 correlated most strongly with the glycolysis composite score (r = 0.675; PAM50-adjusted partial r = 0.575). Conclusions PGK1 varies substantially by breast cancer subtype and remains associated with overall survival after accounting for age, stage, and PAM50 subtype. These exploratory single-cohort findings require independent clinical and experimental validation.

title: A dual-stream Pyramid ViT–ConvFormer architecture leverages dynamic early stopping to classify diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
abstractText: Abstract Purpose: Accurate stratification of Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL) into MYC subtypes is crucial for determining therapeutic intensity. While Vision Transformers (ViTs) excel at capturing global tissue context, their quadratic computational complexity results in slow convergence. To address this, we developed PyConv, a dual-stream network designed to accelerate training while maintaining precise DLBCL classification. Methods: PyConv pairs local ConvFormer blocks with global Pyramid Vision Transformer (PVT) blocks, unifying cytological boundaries and macro-level tissue context via a Multi-Head Cross-Attention fusion layer. The architecture was evaluated using 180 whole-slide images (69,480 testing patches) against 13 state-of-the-art backbones. Results: PyConv achieved a multi-class accuracy and macro F1-score of 0.9962, an absolute decision boundary for benign cohorts, and a malignant stratification AUROC of 0.9999. It reached optimal generalization by epoch 20, an 83.5% reduction in convergence time over pure transformers. While pure hybrid models showed slightly higher raw throughput, DeLong’s testing confirmed performance variances were statistically non-significant. Grad-CAM, Integrated Gradient, and Attention Rollout verified that PyConv correctly prioritizes key cytological features like nuclear contours and prominent nucleoli. Conclusion: PyConv offers a highly accelerated, computationally balanced alternative for DLBCL stratification without sacrificing diagnostic accuracy or clinical interpretability.

title: Numerical study of corrosion-product particle deposition in a trapezoidal rib-wrapped fuel rod channel of a lead-bismuth reactor
Effects of persistent joints on the strain failure of the roof and floor around a circular opening
abstractText: Abstract To investigate localized damage concentration and coalescence-induced instability of surrounding rock where fault fracture zones coexist with roadway excavations, a circular opening was used to represent a roadway or underground cavern, while a through-going filled fissure represented a fault fracture zone or filled weak structural plane. Biaxial compression tests under low lateral confinement were conducted on intact sandstone, sandstone with a single circular opening, and opening–fissure specimens with different fissure inclinations and filling thicknesses. Global deformation, local deformation at the opening roof and floor, and acoustic emission (AE) responses were monitored simultaneously. At a fissure inclination of 15°, increasing the filling thickness from 2 mm to 5 mm and 10 mm increased the peak strength from 43.16 MPa to 48.96 MPa, followed by a slight decrease to 47.90 MPa, while the peak axial deformation generally increased. At a filling thickness of 2 mm, increasing the fissure inclination from 10° to 15° and 20° reduced the peak strength from 53.47 MPa to 43.16 MPa and then increased it to 55.61 MPa, whereas the peak axial deformation first decreased and then increased markedly. These results indicate non-monotonic effects of both fissure inclination and filling thickness. Increasing the filling thickness intensified AE activity during the middle and late loading stages and markedly increased the proportion of shear-type events, which reached 67.5% and 63.9% for the 5 mm and 10 mm specimens, respectively. At a fissure inclination of 20°, the shear-event proportion increased to 21.0%, indicating a transition from tensile-dominated failure to tensile–shear mixed or shear-dominated failure. Considering peak strength, local deformation around the opening, and local instability time, specimen s-15-2 exhibited the strongest deformation concentration and earliest instability, indicating the poorest overall stability, whereas s-15-5 showed relatively high strength, the latest roof instability, and limited floor deformation, indicating comparatively better stability. These findings provide an experimental basis for instability assessment, hazardous-zone delineation, and support optimization for roadways adjacent to fault fracture zones.

A coupled plasma-assisted growth and electrochemical modelling framework for predicting the supercapacitor performance of vertically oriented graphene nanosheets
abstractText: Abstract A coupled plasma-assisted growth and electrochemical modelling framework is developed to establish a quantitative relationship between plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD) operating conditions, vertically oriented graphene nanosheet (VGNS) morphology, and supercapacitor performance. Plasma characteristics obtained from a two-dimensional axisymmetric COMSOL model are coupled with a reduced-order growth model to determine the evolution of nanosheet height, thickness, and electrochemically accessible surface area under different chamber pressures and RF powers. Plasma-induced defect generation and electrochemically active-site formation are further incorporated into the electrochemical model to evaluate the individual contributions of electric double-layer capacitance (EDLC) and pseudocapacitance. The results show that decreasing the chamber pressure and increasing the RF power promote the growth of taller VGNS with a larger electrochemically accessible surface area while simultaneously increasing the density of electrochemically active sites. Consequently, the projected capacitance increases under more energetic plasma conditions, with EDLC remaining the dominant charge-storage mechanism and pseudocapacitance providing an additional contribution through plasma-induced surface activation. The model predicts a maximum projected capacitance of 196 µF cm⁻², which is in good agreement with reported experimental values for plasma-grown VGNS electrodes. The proposed framework provides a physically consistent basis for understanding the coupled effects of plasma processing, graphene growth, and electrochemical behaviour, and offers a practical computational tool for optimizing PECVD conditions for VGNS-based supercapacitor electrodes.

title: Molecular Insights into Gene Expression Changes in Apoptosis Immune Response and Cellular Regulation Pathways in Chronic Kidney Disease Patients
abstractText: Abstract Background : Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a complex, multifactorial disease characterized by the overlapping pathways of apoptosis, immune regulation, and fibrosis, which play a pivotal role in disease progression. However, the molecular integration of these pathways remains incompletely understood, particularly regarding their combined impact on the deterioration of renal function. Methods : The study included 60 participants: 30 patients with CKD and 30 healthy individuals as a control group. Hematological and biochemical parameters, including hemoglobin, hematocrit, urea, creatinine, and glucose, were assessed. Gene expression of CASP8, CASP9, PDCD1, CTLA4, and TGFB3 was analyzed using RT-qPCR, with the 2-ΔΔCt method employed to calculate relative variability. Statistical analyses were performed using comparison tests and correlation analysis. Results : a significant decrease in hemoglobin levels (9.37±0.50 vs. 14.18±0.64 g/dL) and hematocrit (28.63±1.40 vs. 40.69±1.91), compared to a significant increase in urea (124.38±17.39 vs. 29.64±2.25 mg/dL) and creatinine (8.16±0.63 vs. 0.75±0.03 mg/dL) (p<0.001). At the molecular level, significant increases in the gene expression of CASP8 (46.09±6.70 folds) and CASP9 (13.59±1.51 folds) were observed, along with elevated levels of PDCD1 (25.66±4.19), CTLA4 (34.69±8.43), and TGFB3 (15.29±2.83). Conclusion : These findings suggest a complex regulatory network involving apoptosis activation, immunosuppression, and fibrosis in patients with renal failure. These results highlight an integrated molecular axis that may represent a promising target for future therapeutic interventions and provide a foundation for a deeper understanding of the pathogenic mechanisms underlying disease progression.

title: Computational assessment of direct CO2 hydrogenation catalyzed by iron porphyrin
abstractText: Carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions drive climate change, demanding innovative capture and conversion strategies. Catalytic hydrogenation using affordable and abundant catalysts offers a promising route. Using density functional theory, we evaluated iron porphyrins as potential promoters of CO₂ hydrogenation, focusing on the reaction mechanism and the influence of iron oxidation and spin states. Our analysis reveals that the H₂splitting step promoted by Fe²⁺-porphyrin presents the highest barrier in the whole mechanism, yet it remains accessible. The Fe³⁺-porphyrin appears to be more efficient, affording lower barriers. Additionally, a base as cocatalyst is required during the H₂splitting step, while the presence of the conjugate acid of this base is energetically unfavorable when present in the following step, which is the hydride transfer to CO₂. Thus, our calculations suggest that iron porphyrins can effectively promote CO₂ hydrogenation.

title: Association of Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate, Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio, and Platelet-to-Lymphocyte Ratio at the Initiation of Hemodialysis with Mortality
abstractText: Abstract Introduction: In this study, we aimed to retrospectively examine the effects of neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), and glomerular filtration rate (GFR) at the initiation of hemodialysis on mortality in hemodialysis patients. Methods The study was conducted retrospectively on patients who underwent hemodialysis in the province of Hatay between January 2010 and January 2025. Inclusion criteria were being on hemodialysis for at least 3 months and being older than 18 years. Exclusion criteria included home hemodialysis, peritoneal dialysis, age under 18 years, and undergoing hemodialysis for less than 3 months. Results A total of 1136 patients were included in the study. The mean age of the patients was 64.7 ± 13.42 years. The mean GFR at the initiation of hemodialysis was 8.48 ± 3.76 mL/min/1.73 m². No significant association was detected between NLR, PLR, and mortality. According to logistic regression analysis, the independent factors significantly associated with mortality were age, diabetes, and GFR category (p < 0.05). Each one-year increase in age increased the risk of death by 1.031 times (p < 0.001). The risk of death was approximately 1.76 times higher in diabetic patients compared with non-diabetics (p < 0.001). Patients with GFR < 7 mL/min/1.73 m² had 2.53 times higher mortality risk compared with those with GFR > 10 mL/min/1.73 m² (p = 0.008). Conclusion This study demonstrates that age, the presence of diabetes, and low initial GFR are significant determinants of mortality in hemodialysis patients. These findings highlight the importance of early intervention and management of comorbidities in this population.

title: Use of systemic menopausal hormone therapy among French women: a descriptive nationwide study over the 2011 to 2024 period
abstractText: Abstract Background Worldwide use of systemic menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) declined sharply after 2002 following reports of increased breast cancer and cardiovascular risks. Evidence that the benefit-risk balance depends on initiation timing and treatment patterns has renewed clinical interest in MHT recently. A comprehensive characterisation of utilisation patterns is thus needed to assess alignment with guidelines. We describe systemic MHT use among women aged ≥45 years in France between 2011 and 2024. Methods In this descriptive nationwide study using the French National Health Data System (SNDS), we included 21,983,503 women aged ≥45 years affiliated with the main health insurance scheme between 2011 and 2024. Systemic MHT was identified from reimbursements for drugs containing systemic oestrogen. Users had at least two reimbursements for systemic oestrogen (unopposed or with a progestogen) within 12 months, and initiators had no reimbursements in the preceding five years. Annual prevalence, initiation and discontinuation proportions were estimated overall and by age group. Results We identified 1,250,037 systemic MHT users and 578,668 initiators between 2011 and 2024. Annual prevalence decreased from 4.3% in 2011 to 2.0% in 2022, then stabilised, with a slight increase after 2022 among women aged 45-59 years. Prevalence was consistently highest among women aged 55-59 years. Initiation declined from 0.5% of women in 2011 to 0.2% in 2022, before increasing to 0.3% in 2024, and was highest among women aged 50-54 years. Discontinuation was highest among women aged 45-49 years, peaking in 2019, and remained stable in older age groups. Median age at initiation was 52 (Interquartile Range [IQR] 50-55) years, and median treatment duration was 2.1 (IQR 0.6-6.1) years. Most initiators (79.3%) started combined oestrogen-progestogen therapy. Oestradiol was used almost exclusively (98.5%), mainly transdermally (74.2%). Micronised progesterone was the predominant progestogen, used exclusively by 62.9% of combined therapy initiators, followed by dydrogesterone (9.2%). Conclusion After prolonged declining use, systemic MHT initiation increased modestly after 2022. Prescribing appeared broadly aligned with current recommendations favouring transdermal oestradiol combined with micronised progesterone, for relatively short durations. These findings provide a benchmark for public health authorities to monitor alignment between prescribing patterns and guidelines and inform future decisions.

title: Extending AIMNet2 to Macrocyclic Peptides through Data-Efficient Continual Training
abstractText: Abstract Macrocyclic peptides are among the most promising therapeutic modalities, yet no general-purpose machine-learned interatomic potential (MLIP) has been systematically benchmarked for their conformational analysis. We show that on the MPCONF196 macrocyclic benchmark, the four-model AIMNet2 ensemble outperforms MACE-OFF23(S), despite macrocycles being entirely absent from its training data. A single AIMNet2 model is 3- to 5-fold faster and needs 5- to 63-fold less GPU memory than the MACE-OFF23 models at their default float64-precision. The four-model ensemble is about as fast as MACE-OFF23 but retains a 3- to 32-fold memory advantage even against MACE-OFF23 in float32. The larger MACE-OFF23(M) and MACE-OFF23(L) models remain more accurate. To narrow this gap, we introduce a continual training protocol that requires new quantum-chemical labels for fewer than 25,000 domain-specific conformers (<0.13% of the training corpus) while preserving conformational-energy accuracy on nonmacrocyclic molecules. On a sequence-disjoint holdout of unseen CREMP macrocyclic peptides, the resulting model, AIMNet2-macro, reduces conformational energy RMSE by 25 to 27% and DFT force RMSE by 20% (25% on backbone atoms) and improves lowest-energy conformer recovery relative to the original AIMNet2. It retains the conformational-energy accuracy of the original model on the nonmacrocyclic drug-like molecules of CONFORGE and also improves accuracy on the structurally distinct macrocycles of MPCONF196, although this smaller improvement is not statistically significant. Among the ten training strategies compared, only continual training on the combined corpus (AIMNet2-macro) achieves this improvement without degrading small-molecule accuracy. AIMNet2-macro is therefore the best balanced, though not the most accurate, of the models tested. As an independent case study, AIMNet2-macro reproduces DFT conformational energies of six cyclosporine A conformers with an RMSE of 0.78 kcal mol–1 and the correct rank ordering, the lowest error among the MLIPs and semiempirical methods evaluated on this system. The continual training strategy has been adopted in the AIMNet2 (2025) release, which unifies small-molecule, macrocyclic, and intermolecular-interaction treatment in a single production potential.

title: Primary ovarian small-cell carcinoma of pulmonary type: a single-center case series and structured review of published cases
abstractText: Abstract Background Small-cell carcinoma of the ovary, pulmonary type (SCCOPT), is a rare, high-grade neuroendocrine carcinoma with no established standard treatment. We described seven patients treated at our centre and systematically reviewed published patient-level evidence. Methods We retrospectively reviewed seven patients treated between August 2015 and January 2025. PubMed, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, SpringerLink, and Wiley Online Library were searched from inception to 2 August 2026. Eligible reports provided patient-level diagnostic, treatment, follow-up, or outcome data. Published and institutional cases were combined for descriptive, Kaplan–Meier, and exploratory Cox analyses. Results Forty-two studies contributed 76 non-duplicated published patients. With seven institutional patients, the pooled cohort comprised 83 patients. The median age was 55 years (range, 14–85), and 57 of 78 patients with reported stage (73.1%) had FIGO stage III–IV disease. Taxane–platinum and etoposide–platinum exposure were reported in 32 (38.6%) and 24 (28.9%) patients, respectively. CD56, synaptophysin, and chromogranin A were positive in 46/47 (97.9%), 53/59 (89.8%), and 47/66 (71.2%) tested patients. Overall survival data were available for 66 patients; 42 deaths occurred, and the median overall survival was 14.0 months. The estimated 12-, 24-, and 36-month overall survival rates were 61.9%, 33.6%, and 30.2%. Conclusions SCCOPT has an aggressive clinical course and a variable immunophenotype. Surgery and platinum-based chemotherapy remain the main treatment approaches, but current evidence does not establish a preferred regimen. Multicentre registration, central pathological review, and standardised molecular and outcome reporting are needed.

title: Theatre-in-education for preventing illicit substance use among adolescents: protocol for a mixed-methods realist evaluation
abstractText: Background: Illicit substance use remains a significant public health challenge among adolescents in the UK, with prevalence particularly high in areas of South East England. Early intervention is critical for preventing escalation and promoting resilience in young people. Theatre-in-Education offers a promising approach, combining professional theatre performance with structured educational activities to engage students both cognitively and emotionally. Despite its growing use in Personal, Social, Health and Economic education, robust evidence on its effectiveness and mechanisms of action for substance use prevention is limited. Methods: This protocol describes a mixed-methods realist-informed evaluation of a multi-component Theatre-in-Education intervention delivered in secondary schools across East Sussex. The intervention comprises a live theatre performance, lesson plans, a teacher training webinar, and classroom discussions. The evaluation adopts a realist approach to explore not only whether the intervention works, but also how, for whom, and in what contexts. Quantitative data will be collected via pre- and post-intervention questionnaires with pupils and school staff to assess changes in knowledge, refusal self-efficacy, wellbeing, and social influences. Qualitative data will be generated through audience observations, creative pupil focus groups, interviews with school staff, and parent/carer focus groups. Data will be analysed using realist-informed evaluation and triangulation approaches, with integration of findings to develop context–mechanism–outcome configurations. A health economics analysis will be conducted to assess costs and benefits, including value for money. Analysis will also be carried out to assess potential impact on health inequalities. Discussion: This evaluation aims to provide vital evidence on the effectiveness, execution, and equity of Theatre-in-Education as a strategy for preventing illicit substance use in adolescence. By examining both outcomes and underlying mechanisms, the study will inform future adaptation and scale-up of arts-based interventions in drug education and contribute to understanding how best to support young people’s health and wellbeing in diverse school contexts. The involvement of young people, school staff, and parents as active research partners ensures the study is responsive to real-world needs and settings. Trial registration: The study was registered with the ISRCTN registry (ISRCTN52466797) on 24/04/2025.

title: A Cross-Sectional Study in Northeast India to Assess Malaria, Scrub Typhus, and Dengue in Patients with Acute Febrile Illness Using ELISA
abstractText: Abstract Aim Acute febrile illness (AFI) is a major reason for hospitalization in tropical and subtropical regions. Overlapping clinical features might also lead to confusion about the diagnosis of AFI. In India, dengue, scrub typhus, and malaria continue to be the most prevalent causes. Early laboratory validation using ELISA-based assays is essential for timely medication and a reduction in morbidity and death. Methods Using commercial ELISA kits to detect dengue NS1 antigen, dengue IgM antibodies, scrub typhus IgM antibodies, and malaria pLDH antigen in accordance with manufacturer instructions, a cross-sectional study of 200 patients presenting with AFI—95 urban and 105 rural residents—was carried out. Data on demographics, residential status, and length of fever were recorded, and statistical analysis was carried out using PAST software. Result The results showed that 51% of the patients were male and 49% were female. Patients from rural areas made up a higher proportion (53%) than those from metropolitan areas (47%). 16% of patients in cities were positive for dengue NS1, 7% for dengue IgM, 12% for scrub typhus, and 17% for malaria. Dengue (18%), scrub typhus (19%), and malaria (22%) were more prevalent among rural people. Longer fevers, particularly those lasting between 6 and 14 days, were related to greater positives. Malaria and scrub typhus were the leading causes of AFI. Conclusion ELISA-based diagnostics are useful for early detection of AFI etiology. Higher rural incidence highlights the importance of improved monitoring, early diagnostic access, and focused public health interventions.

title: Processing of Garlic and Lemon as a Supplement in The Village of Meureubo
abstractText: Food supplements are finished products consumed to supplement daily meals. Health foods are derived from natural ingredients without chemicals and are derived from herbal ingredients. Herbal supplements are one of the products that are consumed externally and have high antioxidant activity to prevent free radicals in the body. Garlic and lemon contain antioxidants that can support the body's defense mechanisms. This community service activity aims to introduce and explain the processing techniques of garlic and lemon as beverage supplements to the people of Meurebo Village. The Community Service method used is to first describe the types of ingredients and their functions that will be used as raw materials for supplements, then explain the correct formulation of garlic and lemon to produce a good supplement. Then, the practice of making herbal supplements. Listening to the presentation of material and practice of making beverage supplements by the speaker, the community gained a better understanding of the benefits and processing technology of garlic and lemon for health. In general, the community also understood the role and function of agricultural commodity processing technology for food products in meeting food and public health needs.

title: Propulsion systems for a starshade rendezvous mission with the Habitable World Observatory
abstractText: We assess how propulsion and operational constraints shape the exo-Earth characterization performance of a starshade rendezvous architecture for a Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO)–like telescope at Sun–Earth L2. Using end-to-end Monte Carlo mission simulations with EXOSIMS, we model two representative starshade point designs: a 60 m occulter optimized for visible-band (VIS) spectroscopy (500 to 1000 nm) and a 35 m occulter optimized for near-ultraviolet (NUV) characterization (250 to 550 nm). For the 60 m case, we compare three electric-propulsion options spanning Hall and gridded-ion technologies (AEPS Hall, NEXT ion, and a Starlink-class Hall system) and quantify yield sensitivity to onboard propellant capacity, retargeting trajectory “burn-portion” (accelerate and decelerate fraction of slew), and the presence or absence of on-orbit refueling. In fuel-limited scenarios (1000 to 3000 kg initial propellant), the higher-Isp NEXT system delivers the largest characterization yield, providing 9% to 13% more characterizations than AEPS and 13% to 16% more than the Starlink-class option by enabling more retargeting slews per kilogram of propellant. When refueling is allowed, cumulative yields converge across thruster choices (about 120 cumulative characterizations over a 10-year campaign), while the propulsion choice primarily trades against the number of refueling events. For the 35 m near-UV starshade (modeled with AEPS), yields are substantially less fuel-sensitive and are instead dominated by mission time and geometric accessibility; tightening the minimum solar keepout (scarf) angle from 40 deg toward ≥50 deg barely impacts yield, from 50 deg to 65 deg modestly impacts yield, and ≥65 deg reduces yield rapidly, with severe degradation near 80 deg. These results identify regimes where starshade performance is fundamentally fuel-limited versus time/keepout-limited and provide quantitative guidance for jointly optimizing propulsion selection, tank size, refueling policy, and keepout constraints in HWO starshade architectures.

title: Interconnected Mental Health Stressors and Risks in Returnee Nepalese Migrant Workers: A Focus Group Study
abstractText: Abstract For Nepalese migrant workers, working abroad can negatively affect their mental health and well-being. Studies on labour migrants have documented poor occupational health outcomes, both mental and physical. However, research into their sources of stress, coping mechanisms, and suicidal thoughts remains limited. This qualitative study explored the sources of stress and perceived risks to mental health in returnee Nepalese migrant workers. We conducted seven focus groups (five male, one female and one mixed gender) with returnee migrants from Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries and Malaysia. Participants were purposively recruited with support from local health workers and community organisations working for migrants. Over half had worked abroad for at least five years, with an average of 7.7 years. Our analysis identified six themes: (1) accommodation and communication; (2) occupational health; (3) exploitation at work; (4) family at home; (5) leisure, coping and risk behaviours; and (6) suicide narratives and mental health support, all six are linked to social determinants of mental health. These interconnected themes can negatively impact the mental health and well-being of migrant workers. Gender disparities and limited mental health support available abroad, including suicide prevention strategies, further intensify these challenges. Since this study focuses on returnees, workers currently abroad might have different experiences. Overall, our findings underscore the need for targeted support and interventions to improve the mental health and well-being of Nepalese migrant workers. We recommend establishing longitudinal studies to inform policy and practice related to mental health.

title: Implementasi Program Jumat Berkah sebagai Strategi Penguatan Kepedulian Sosial Mahasiswa KKN Melalui Aksi Berbagai di Kelurahan Curahgrinting Kota Probolinggo
abstractText: Program Jumat Berkah merupakan salah satu bentuk pengabdian kepada masyarakat yang bertujuan menumbuhkan kepedulian sosial melalui aksi berbagi. Artikel ini bertujuan mendeskripsikan pelaksanaan program Jumat Berkah sebagai upaya penguatan kepedulian sosial mahasiswa Kuliah Kerja Nyata (KKN) di Kelurahan Curahgrinting, Kota Probolinggo. Kegiatan dilaksanakan pada 11 September 2026 melalui penyaluran paket makanan kepada lima kelompok sasaran, yaitu pengemis, penarik becak, tukang parkir, pengatur jalan atau pak ogah, serta lansia. Sebanyak 50 paket makanan direncanakan untuk disalurkan dengan alokasi 10 paket bagi setiap kelompok. Pelaksanaan kegiatan mencakup perencanaan, persiapan kebutuhan, pengemasan makanan, pembagian tugas, penyaluran bantuan, serta evaluasi kegiatan. Pendekatan partisipatif digunakan untuk menggambarkan keterlibatan mahasiswa dalam setiap tahapan program. Data pelaksanaan didasarkan pada pengamatan langsung, catatan kegiatan, dan dokumentasi. Program ini berpotensi menjadi sarana pembelajaran sosial bagi mahasiswa dalam menerapkan nilai empati, solidaritas, gotong royong, dan tanggung jawab. Namun, peningkatan kepedulian sosial dan manfaat langsung bagi penerima belum dapat dipastikan tanpa data evaluasi yang lebih terukur. Oleh karena itu, dokumentasi dan evaluasi yang sistematis diperlukan untuk mendukung penilaian keberhasilan program.

title: Pemberdayaan UMKM Potong Babi melalui Transformasi Pemasaran Digital dan Edukasi Lingkungan di Desa Darmasaba
abstractText: Usaha Mikro, Kecil, dan Menengah (UMKM) berperan penting dalam perekonomian desa, tetapi pengembangannya perlu didukung oleh pemasaran digital dan kepedulian lingkungan. Kegiatan Proyek Desa di Desa Darmasaba bertujuan mendukung UMKM potong babi melalui pendampingan pemasaran digital dan edukasi pengelolaan limbah berbasis Tri Hita Karana. Identifikasi terhadap 10 UMKM menunjukkan bahwa sebagian besar masih mengandalkan pemasaran langsung dan belum optimal memanfaatkan media sosial. Pendampingan diberikan kepada tiga UMKM melalui pembuatan logo, penataan akun Instagram dan TikTok, serta pembuatan konten promosi. Sementara itu, edukasi lingkungan kepada 10 pelaku UMKM mencakup pemilahan sampah, pembuatan eco-enzyme, pemanfaatan kotoran babi sebagai kompos, dan kebersihan lingkungan. Kegiatan ini diharapkan mendukung promosi usaha sekaligus meningkatkan kesadaran terhadap pengelolaan limbah yang bertanggung jawab.
