title: Strategi Komunikasi Pemasaran pada Busrain Coffee & Eatery Lhokseumawe
abstractText: Persaingan usaha coffee shop mendorong pelaku usaha untuk menerapkan strategi komunikasi pemasaran yang efektif dalam menarik perhatian dan membangun hubungan dengan konsumen. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis strategi komunikasi pemasaran Busrain Coffee & Eatery Lhokseumawe berdasarkan empat tahapan model AIDA, yaitu Attention, Interest, Desire, dan Action, serta mengidentifikasi hambatan dalam pelaksanaannya. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif. Informan berjumlah tujuh orang yang terdiri atas satu manajer, lima konsumen, dan satu barista yang ditentukan melalui teknik purposive sampling. Data dikumpulkan melalui observasi, wawancara mendalam, dan dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan model Miles dan Huberman. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa tahap Attention dilakukan melalui promosi Instagram, TikTok, dan rekomendasi dari mulut ke mulut. Tahap Interest dibangun melalui suasana tempat yang nyaman, variasi menu, dan pelayanan. Tahap Desire diperkuat melalui informasi serta rekomendasi produk dari barista dan konsumen lain. Tahap Action terlihat dari pembelian, pemesanan ulang, kunjungan kembali, dan rekomendasi kepada orang lain. Pelaksanaannya masih menghadapi hambatan teknis, semantik, dan psikologis. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa kombinasi promosi digital, komunikasi interpersonal, dan pengalaman konsumen menjadi unsur penting dalam mendukung efektivitas komunikasi pemasaran Busrain Coffee & Eatery.

title: Antiplasmodial-guided Isolation from Organic Extracts of the Root Bark of Detarium microcarpum Guill. & Perr.
abstractText: In Niger, malaria remains a major public health problem, representing a leading cause of morbidity and mortality, particularly in children under five. Traditional medicine have significant importance, as it is often the first line of treatment due to its accessibility, cultural acceptability, and low cost. This study focused on the extraction, characterization, and antiplasmodial evaluation of bioactive compounds derived from the root bark of Detarium microcarpum. Successive extractions were performed using two solvents: methanol (100%) and a mixture of methanol and dichloromethane (1 :1). The obtained extracts were screened on chloroquine-sensitive (Pf3D7) and multidrug-resistant (PfDd2) P. falciparum strains using SyBr Green method. The most active dichloromethane-methanol extract (Pf3D7: IC50 = 11.98 ± 0.52 µg/mL and PfDd2: IC50 = 14.02 ± 0.17 µg/mL) was fractionated through liquid-liquid separation using n-hexane, ethyl acetate, and n-butanol. The ethyl acetate fraction yielded three isolated steroids (1-3) and two triterpenoids (4-5). Compound (5), identified as oleanolic acid, exhibited the highest activity (Pf3D7: IC50 = 4.82 ± 0.42 µg/mL and PfDd2: IC50 = 7.02 ± 0.27 µg/mL). Comprehensive analyses including phytochemical screening, chromatographic purification, spectral interpretation, and antiplasmodial activity assessment highlighted the chemical and pharmacological potential of the organic extracts. The overall results suggest that this plant is a promising source of molecules with therapeutic potential, especially for in vitro antiplasmodial activity. This work thus constitutes a significant contribution to the scientific valorization of local plant and opens up new possibilities for the development of phytomedicines derived from the African pharmacopoeia.

Early spine surgery is associated with better outcomes in patients with a thoracic spinal cord injury: national database retrospective analysis
abstractText: Abstract Introduction We aim to determine whether early surgery (within 24 h of admission) is associated with better discharge disposition in patients with isolated and polytraumatic thoracic SCI. Methods Patients in the Trauma Quality and Improvement Database from 2017 to 2023 presenting with a thoracic SCI and underwent surgical intervention were collected based on Abbreviated Injury Scale (AIS) codes and ICD-10 procedural codes. Polytrauma was determined as those patients presenting with an AIS ≥ 3 in a body region not associated with thoracic SCI and GCS < 14. Propensity score matching (PSM) was conducted to match early and late surgery groups for isolated SCI and polytrauma separately. Univariate analysis was conducted to determine differences in hospital complications and disposition. Multivariate logistic regression for disposition was modelled. Multivariate regression using the propensity matched data with a 3-level time to surgery variable (< 8 h, 8–24 h, 24 + hours) was modelled. Results After PSM there were 4,524 isolated and 2,842 polytrauma thoracic SCI patients. The isolated and polytrauma SCI group with early surgery had lower rates of hospital complications. Isolated SCI patients with late surgery had 22% (95% CI: 4%-42%) higher odds of poor disposition. Polytrauma patients with late surgery had 42% (95% CI: 18%-70%) higher odds of poor disposition. Isolated thoracic SCI patients undergoing surgery 8–24 h after admission had a 32% (95% CI: 4%-68%) increase in odds of poor disposition compared to those undergoing surgery within 8 h of admission. Conclusion Early surgery in patients presenting with an isolated thoracic SCI or polytrauma with thoracic SCI was associated with more positive discharge dispositions.

title: Microwear analysis on Pinctada margaritifera tattooing combs from Central East Polynesia
abstractText: Pearl shell tattooing combs form a small corpus in the material culture in Central East Polynesia, providing evidence for traditional methods of tattooing and body modification, and represent a significant form of cultural practice in ancient island communities. Three combs were analysed with microwear analysis, shedding light on manufacturing techniques and use, with an additional four combs analysed macroscopically. This is the first microwear study on pearl shell artefacts in the Pacific, and the results contribute to the wider corpus on microwear traces on pearl shell artefacts and tattooing implements, shedding new light on their chaîne opératoire.

title: Design And Development Of A Web-Based Digital Credit Service And Qris Transaction System
abstractText: The rapid development of financial technology (fintech) has accelerated the adoption of digital payment and digital credit services. However, most digital credit services still rely on cash disbursement mechanisms, making it difficult to control the utilization of borrowed funds. This study aims to develop PayQRIS, a web-based Buy Now, Pay Later (PayLater) service integrated with QRIS payments that enables cashless transactions using credit limits without direct cash disbursement. The system was developed using the Prototyping model and evaluated through black-box testing and the System Usability Scale (SUS). The results show that PayQRIS successfully integrates PayLater services with QRIS payments into a single platform featuring credit limit determination, installment and bill management, bill extension, and secure transaction authentication. Functional testing confirmed that all system features operated according to the specified requirements, while the usability evaluation produced a SUS score of 83.25, indicating a high level of usability and user acceptance. Therefore, PayQRIS provides a web-based PayLater solution that supports QRIS payments through a more controlled digital credit mechanism.

title: Trend analysis of lifetime sexual activity and condom use self-efficacy in repeated cross-sectional survey data among adolescents in the Northwest Territories, Canada
abstractText: Background Evidence of declining condom use over time among adolescents across diverse settings underscores the need to understand sexual health indicators among this population. Few studies have examined trends in lifetime sexual activity and condom use self-efficacy over time among adolescents in Arctic or remote settings. This study assessed changes and sociodemographic patterns in these outcomes across 7 years among Northern and Indigenous adolescents in the Northwest Territories, Canada. Methods We conducted repeated cross-sectional surveys among secondary school students aged 13–18 years across 17 Northwest Territories communities from 2018 to 2024. Outcomes included lifetime sexual activity (ever having engaged in vaginal, anal or oral sex) and condom use self-efficacy. Linear and logistic mixed-effects regression models estimated unadjusted and adjusted associations with time, gender, sexual orientation, Indigenous identity, and rural residence, including interaction terms. Results Among n = 2745 participants (mean age 13.68 years, standard deviation 1.49; gender: 45.65% cisgender girls, 50.27% cisgender boys and 4.08% gender diverse), 19.06% identified as lesbian, gay, bisexual or queer (LGBQ), 72.62% as Indigenous and 71.17% lived in rural settings. From 2018 to 2024, condom use self-efficacy decreased (adjusted beta coefficient −0.25; 95% CI: −0.36, −0.15; P < 0.001), and was lower among LGBQ and rural youth. Sexual activity also declined (adjusted beta coefficient −0.01; 95% CI: −0.02, −0.01; P < 0.001), but remained higher among cisgender girls, LGBQ youth, Indigenous adolescents and rural youth. Conclusion Condom use self-efficacy and sexual activity declined over time, with persistent disparities across groups. Findings highlight the need for sustained, culturally grounded, equity-focused sexual health programming for Northwest Territories adolescents.

title: Pembuatan Konten Video Iklan di Reels Instagram untuk Meningkatkan Engagement pada UMKM Roti Bakar dan Leker Kota Malang
abstractText: Roti Bakar Compol and Leker, a micro, small, and medium enterprise (MSME), has operated for the past five years, focusing on the sale of light meals and snacks. However, the business has not yet optimized the use of Instagram Reels video content, resulting in a relatively low engagement rate, while promotional activities still rely primarily on photos and Instagram Stories. Based on these conditions, this study addresses two research questions: how to develop promotional video content for Instagram Reels and how to measure the engagement generated by the published video content. Accordingly, this study aims to develop promotional video content using CapCut Pro for Instagram Reels, as well as to analyze and measure the resulting engagement as an effort to enhance the effectiveness of digital promotion for Roti Bakar Compol and Leker. This study employed an action research approach based on the Spiral Model, which consisted of four phases: planning, action, observation, and reflection. Data were collected through observations, interviews, questionnaires, and documentation. The collected data were analyzed using the EPIC Model to evaluate the effectiveness of the promotional video content. The study applied purposive sampling and involved 30 respondents, consisting of one business owner, two marketing experts, two computer design experts, fifteen prospective customers, and ten existing customers The results showed that Instagram Reels was highly effective as a promotional medium, achieving an EPIC Model score of (4.4), which was classified as *very effective*. The Communication, Persuasion, and Impact dimensions each obtained a score of (4.4), while the Empathy dimension achieved a score of (4.3), indicating that the promotional video effectively communicated the marketing message, attracted audience interest, created a positive impression, and fostered audience engagement. The findings indicate that Instagram Reels video content is highly effective in increasing engagement while serving as an effective promotional medium for Roti Bakar Compol and Leker, Malang. The study recommends that the business adopt the developed video content as a promotional blueprint, maintain a consistent posting schedule, and adapt the content for other digital marketing platforms. It is also recommended that the Marketing Department regularly update its design software and practical learning resources to align with current industry standards and better prepare students for the professional workplace.

title: Effect of aging on marginal and internal adaptation of bulk-fill resin composites with different viscosities in class II restorations
abstractText: Abstract Aim To evaluate and compare the effect of thermocycling and water storage on the marginal and internal adaptation of bulk-fill resin composites with different viscosities (No-cap low viscosity, thermoviscous, sonically activated, and conventional bulk-fill) in Class II restorations using scanning electron microscope. Materials and methods Fifty-six sound molars were prepared with standardized class II cavities (occlusal depth:3.0 mm, bucco-lingual width: 3.0 mm, depth, proximal box: 3.0 mm bucco-lingual width, 1.5 mm axial depth, and gingival margin extended 1-mm below CEJ). They were assigned into four groups according to the material used ( n = 14). For the marginal and internal adaptation test, half of the specimens in each group were tested after one week, however the remaining half were tested after 12 months of water storage and exposure to 10,000 thermal cycles between 5 and 55 °C. Replicas were made and evaluated for marginal and internal adaptation using a scanning electron microscope at different magnifications. Continuous margin percentage values (%CM) and Maximum gap width values (MGW) were statistically analyzed. Results Aging did not significantly affect external % CM, internal % CM, or external MGW ( p > 0.05). However, internal MGW values were significantly lower in immediate specimens compared with aged ones ( p < 0.05). Among the tested composites, no significant differences were observed in external or internal % CM or external MGW ( p > 0.05). Nevertheless, at the dentin gingival margin, lower-viscosity bulk-fill composites generally showed numerically lower internal MGW values than the high-viscosity bulk-fill composite. However, after Bonferroni adjustment, statistically significant differences were observed only between Flowable and Tetric and between SonicFill and Tetric ( p < 0.05). Furthermore, a strong correlation was detected between external and internal adaptation parameters (%CM and MGW) ( p < 0.05). Conclusion Aging did not adverse effect %CM or external MGW but significantly increased internal MGW. Some lower-viscosity bulk-fill composites showed lower internal MGW values at the gingival margin than the high-viscosity composite under the conditions of this in vitro study.

title: Comparative assessment of freshly cultured microbial bioproducts and a seaweed-based biostimulant for plant growth promotion and root-knot nematode management in capsicum and spinach in Kenya
abstractText: Summary Root-knot nematodes (RKN; Meloidogyne spp.) are among the most damaging pathogens of vegetable crops worldwide. They damage roots and reduce yield, with their management becoming challenging because of their wide host range. This study evaluated three microbial bioproducts, Mytech ® ( Purpureocillium lilacinum ), Trichotech ® ( Trichoderma asperellum ) and Regain ® ( Bacillus subtilis ) and a seaweed-based biostimulant (Maximizer ® ) for growth promotion and RKN management in capsicum and spinach. The fungal and bacterial bioproducts were cultured to provide fresh inocula for each experimental trial. In RKN-free pot experiments, Mytech ® and Trichotech ® consistently improved plant height, shoot and root fresh weight and total plant weight in capsicum, whereas Regain ® and Mytech ® enhanced plant height, shoot fresh weight and total plant weight in spinach compared with the non-treated control. In RKN-infected pot experiments, where microbial bioproducts or the seaweed-based biostimulant were applied before nematode inoculation, all treatments using bioproducts and biostimulant improved growth parameters, although responses varied between crops and repeated experiments. All bioproducts and biostimulant treatments significantly reduced nematode infection in both crops. However, significant reductions in nematode density, number of galls and reproduction factor were observed only with Regain ® and Mytech ® in spinach. These findings indicate that microbial bioproducts and seaweed-based biostimulants can promote vegetable growth and reduce RKN infection, although their effects on nematode density are treatment- and crop-dependent. Further field validation of these products is needed to establish their effects on marketable yield and economic returns under farmer conditions.

title: Factors Associated with Pre Exposure Prophylaxis Self-Efficacy Among Men Who Have Sex With Men in the United States
abstractText: Abstract Self-efficacy (SE) is central to sexual health behavior change and may be important for pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) adherence among men who have sex with men (MSM). This study examines factors associated with three PrEP self-efficacy domains: routine adherence (RA), medication management (MM), and overcoming psychosocial challenges (OPC). Three hundred U.S. MSM, who either initiated daily oral PrEP or reported anticipated adherence difficulties, and who all experienced at least one psychosocial syndemic condition, were recruited as part of a randomized controlled trial. Baseline assessments included PrEP SE and psychosocial, structural, and sociodemographic variables. Bayesian variable selection and multiple linear regression identified several predictors. Younger age (RA: b = 0.048, 95% CI [0.025, 0.072]; MM: b = 0.033, 95% CI [0.012, 0.054]; OPC: b = 0.060, 95% CI [0.023, 0.087]) and greater structural barriers (RA: b = − 0.090, 95% CI [-0.151, − 0.029]; MM: b = − 0.192, 95% CI [-0.246, − 0.138]; OPC: b = − 0.145, 95% CI [-0.229, − 0.055]) were associated with decreased SE across all factors ( p < .01). Social anxiety was associated with lower routine adherence SE ( b = − 0.039, 95% CI [-0.063, -0.016], p < .01); lifetime polysubstance use was associated with lower medication management SE ( b = − 0.192, 95% CI [-0.325, -0.058], p < .01); and overseas-born status ( b = − 0.932, 95% CI [-1.759, -0.106], p < .05) and greater sexual compulsivity ( b = − 0.157, 95% CI [-0.269, -0.046], p < .01) were both associated with lower SE in overcoming psychosocial challenges. Findings underscore the need for multilevel, culturally responsive PrEP interventions that promote SE across all three domains.

title: Comparative efficacy and safety of locking intramedullary nails versus locking plates for displaced proximal humeral fractures
abstractText: Aims The optimal fixation method for displaced proximal humeral fractures (PHFs) remains debated. Locking intramedullary nails (INs) are considered theoretically less invasive than locking plates (LPs), yet randomized evidence comparing their safety and functional outcomes is inconsistent. This study compares IN and LP using trial sequential analysis (TSA) and complexity-stratified subgroups to determine whether current randomized evidence is sufficient to draw firm conclusions. Methods A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science was conducted from database inception through to January 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing IN and LP in adults with displaced PHFs were included. Primary outcomes were patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) across early (three months), mid-term, and long-term intervals, alongside complication rates. TSA was applied to control for random errors and estimate the required information sizes. Results Six RCTs involving 382 participants were included. At early follow-up, no significant differences in PROMs or pain scores were observed, refuting the expected immediate muscle-sparing advantage of IN. At 12 months, no significant differences were observed between IN and LP in Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder and Hand (DASH) questionnaire score (p = 0.42), Constant-Murley Score (p = 0.55), or American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons score (p = 0.34). At long-term follow-up ≥ 24 months, LP demonstrated statistically lower DASH scores (p = 0.03); however, the difference did not exceed the minimal clinically important difference. Crucially, complexity-stratified analyses revealed a directional signal favouring LP specifically in three- and four-part fractures. TSA showed conclusive evidence that IN does not reduce reoperation rates (risk ratio 1.45; p = 0.58) or screw-related complications compared with LP. Conclusion While pooled evidence demonstrates overarching equivalence, implant selection should be guided by fracture complexity. For two-part surgical neck fractures, either implant is highly appropriate. For displaced three- and four-part fractures, a directional signal from stratified analyses, and the clinical burden of reoperations suggest a potential advantage for LPs. This signal should inform clinical decision-making pending adequately powered, fracture-stratified RCTs. Cite this article: Bone Jt Open 2026;7(11):1419–1428.

title: A tumor-associated K318N variant abolishes AGGF1 nuclear import by disrupting key nucleocytoplasmic transport motifs
abstractText: Abstract Aberrant nucleocytoplasmic transport is linked to tumorigenesis. AGGF1 exerts nuclear tumor-suppressing functions, yet how its nuclear import is regulated remains unclear. Through deletion mapping and point mutations, we identified three motifs (272–279, 317–328 and 509–519 aa) governing AGGF1 nucleocytoplasmic distribution. Knockdown of importin β1 and inhibition of importin α1 showed that the importin α1/β1 complex is the primary nuclear import receptor. GST pull-down assays revealed that 317–328 aa and 509–519 aa, but not 272–279 aa, are required for efficient binding to importin α1. None of the three motifs alone was sufficient to efficiently drive nuclear import, whereas the combined 272–328 aa region conferred robust nuclear import. The tumor-associated K318N variant, within 317–328 aa, is absent from gnomAD and causes profound, cell-type-independent cytoplasmic mislocalization that is not attributable to enhanced CRM1-mediated nuclear export or 14-3-3α/β-dependent cytoplasmic distribution. Consequently, K318N fails to bind nuclear p53, stabilize p53, or activate its transcription, impairing AGGF1 tumor-suppressing function. RNA-seq showed K318-dependent genes enriched in Rap1 signaling, cytoskeleton regulation, and cardiac muscle morphogenesis, suggesting a predominantly loss-of-function effect. These findings identify key motifs and the nuclear import receptor for AGGF1, and reveal how a single variant disrupts nuclear localization and p53 regulation, potentially contributing to tumorigenesis.

Interfacial Stabilization of Highly Concentrated Perfluorohexanone-in-Water Emulsions by Alkyl Polyglycosides
abstractText: Abstract Perfluorohexanone (C6F12O) is a fluorinated liquid that is both hydrophobic and oleophobic, resulting in poor compatibility with conventional hydrocarbon-based surfactants and making its emulsification in water challenging. Herein, emulsions with a high content of internal C6F12O phase (C6F12O/water mass ratio of 8:2) stabilized by alkyl polyglycosides (APGs) were constructed with improved interfacial stabilization. Interfacial tension analysis, Gibbs adsorption fitting, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations reveal that APG12 forms a dense and ordered adsorption layer at the C6F12O–water interface, resulting in enhanced interfacial stability and facilitating emulsification. The obtained emulsion exhibits uniform submicron droplets and excellent storage stability, as reflected by its low apparent droplet coarsening rate. The aqueous continuous phase effectively suppresses the premature volatilization of C6F12O and facilitates its transport and retention during applications. As a proof of concept, fire suppression tests show that the emulsion slightly shortens the extinguishing time (from 10.02 to 9.82 s) while reducing agent consumption by 7%. This work provides insights into the interfacial stabilization and delivery of volatile fluorinated liquids through emulsion construction using conventional hydrocarbon surfactants.

title: Increasing Chlamydia/Gonorrhea Screening in Adolescents Across a Multisite Primary Care Network
abstractText: OBJECTIVE To increase chlamydia and gonorrhea (CT/GC) screening among sexually active female adolescents in a large pediatric primary care network using a multifaceted quality improvement (QI) intervention, with secondary aims to increase male screening and case detection. METHODS From 2021 to 2025, we implemented a sequential QI intervention including Adolescent Health Questionnaire implementation, financial incentives, electronic health record (EHR) best practice advisories, and universal screening protocols across 33 practices. The primary outcome was CT/GC screening rates for sexually active female patients aged at least 15 years at well visits. Secondary outcomes included male screening rates and case detection rates. We evaluated outcomes using statistical process control and run charts. RESULTS During the study period, 136 241 adolescents aged 15–19 years received care across the network, with monthly well care visits increasing over time (average 1472-1681 visits/month). CT/GC screening rates for sexually active female patients increased from approximately 25% to 75%, with the most substantial improvements following universal opt-out protocols. Male testing rates similarly increased from approximately 20% to 75%. Monthly chlamydia case counts for female patients increased from approximately 8 cases/month to a peak of approximately 25 cases/month during the highest-volume testing period. For male patients, cases increased from approximately 4 to 16 monthly. Improvements occurred across demographic groups regardless of insurance type, race, or ethnicity. CONCLUSIONS A systematic, EHR-enabled QI intervention significantly improved adolescent CT/GC screening rates while increasing case detection. Universal opt-out screening protocols proved most effective in achieving comprehensive screening and identifying previously undiagnosed infections, demonstrating the clinical value of systematic CT/GC screening in pediatric primary care.

Uncrewed aircraft systems for blood transport in Kenya: a facility location, utilization, and cost-efficiency analysis
abstractText: Abstract Background Uncrewed aircraft systems (UAS) are increasingly promoted to improve access to blood and emergency medical commodities in low-and middle-income countries. However, economic evaluations have mostly focused on aircraft performance, with limited attention to base station placement, utilization, and staffing requirements – key determinants of unit cost given high fixed operating expenses. Moreover, blood and similar commodities can only be administered in facilities that are legally authorized and clinically equipped to manage severe adverse reactions, constraining effective demand. We evaluated how these factors would jointly affect the cost-efficiency of UAS blood transport in Kenya. Methods We conducted a facility location and economic analysis of UAS blood transport under three base station placement scenarios: existing blood bank sites, urban centers (> 30,000 population), and unrestricted village and town locations. We estimated geographic and population-weighted coverage of transfusing hospitals, compared UAS flight times with road travel times within identical service areas, and projected delivery volumes and unit costs using facility catchment populations, utilization assumptions, and staffing models consistent with 24/7 emergency operations. Results Across scenarios, three base stations covered 50% of transfusing hospitals and 60–81% of national blood demand when weighted by population. Seven stations would cover 75% of transfusing facilities, and 93% of population demand, beyond which marginal gains diminished sharply. Mean UAS delivery time was approximately one-third of road travel time, with the largest advantage observed in urban and peri-urban corridors – precisely where straight-line distance alone would suggest UAS offer limited benefit. Estimated annual base station costs were US$61,500 [95% CI $58,200: $106,000], of which staffing accounted for 59%-84% of costs. The estimated UAS transport costs per unit of whole blood transported was $7.59 [95% CI $5.4: $34.22], compared to $0.78[95% CI $0.63: $1.01] for road transport under our base assumptions of three units delivered per flight. Achieving complete geographic coverage would require approximately 28 stations, many operating at low utilization and high cost. Conclusions In Kenya, a small number of well-placed UAS base stations can achieve substantial gains in hospital access and delivery speed relative to road transport, particularly in dense urban and peri-urban corridors. UAS blood transport is most cost-efficient when concentrated in a limited number of high-utilization stations; staffing, rather than aircraft costs, dominates expenditure and explains why expansion into low-demand areas rapidly increases unit costs. These cost-efficiency findings should be weighed alongside access and equity value of UAS in remote areas, which this analysis does not capture.

abstractText: ABSTRACT Outpatient waiting time is a quality indicator that reflects the organization of service flow and hospital responsiveness. This study aimed to analyze the associations of administrative compliance, discipline, and proactive behavior with compliance with outpatient waiting-time standards among BPJS patients at Pertamina Jaya Hospital. A quantitative approach with a cross-sectional design was employed. The sample consisted of 106 outpatients covered by BPJS, selected using accidental sampling from a population of 2,500 patients. Data were collected through observations of administrative completeness, punctuality of arrival, Mobile JKN use, and service duration, and were analyzed using multiple logistic regression at a significance level of 0.05. The results showed that most patients experienced waiting times exceeding 60 minutes. The regression model was statistically significant overall, with a Nagelkerke R² of 0.458 and a classification accuracy of 83.0%. Administrative compliance and discipline were significantly associated with compliance with the waiting-time standard, whereas proactive behavior did not show a statistically significant partial association. Discipline was the most prominent variable in the model based on its odds ratio and statistical significance. These findings indicate the need to strengthen information about administrative requirements, improve patient arrival-time management, and evaluate the integration of Mobile JKN with the hospital’s queuing and appointment scheduling systems to support more orderly and efficient outpatient services. Chemical composition, antioxidant and antibiofilm actions of Salvia rosmarinus and Plinia cauliflora extracts against endodontic pathogens and cytotoxicity on human Keratinocytes
abstractText: Abstract The ongoing search for new endodontic irrigants is critical due to the persistence of resistant microorganisms within the root canal system. This study evaluated the hydroethanolic extracts of Salvia rosmarinus (rosemary) and Plinia cauliflora (jabuticaba) for their chemical composition, antioxidant activity, synergistic and antibiofilm effects against a clinical strain of Enterococcus faecalis and standard strains of Porphyromonas gingivalis and Fusobacterium nucleatum . Additionally, their cytotoxicity was tested on human keratinocytes (HaCaT). The extracts were prepared and filtered. The content of soluble solids, flavonoids, and phenols were quantified. High-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) was performed later. The minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) and minimum bactericidal concentration (MBC) were evaluated. Then, the free radical suppressive (antioxidant) activity and the synergistic activity of the extract’s combination using checkerboard microdilution assay were evaluated. The most effective concentrations were analyzed against biofilms. Later, the cytotoxicity of the extracts was tested on human keratinocyte lines (HaCaT). Data were analyzed by the Kruskal Wallis and Dunn test (p ≤ 0.05). S. rosmarinus extract contained 9.48 mg/mL of soluble solids and was rich in caffeoylquinic and chlorogenic acids. P. cauliflora had 22.22 mg/mL of soluble solids, with gallic and ellagic acids as major compounds. Both extracts demonstrated antioxidant activity at 59 μg/mL for S. rosmarinus and 159 μg/mL for P. cauliflora . An additive antibacterial effect was observed against E. faecalis when 0.036 mg/mL of S. rosmarinus was combined with 2.77 mg/mL of P. cauliflora . Both extracts at low concentrations did not reduce the metabolic activity of HaCaT cells.

title: Teacher Strategies for Social Studies Learning under A Shift System in Tuah Kemuning Sencalang
abstractText: This study analyzed teachers’ strategies and teaching methods for Social Studies learning under a shift system at SMAN Tuah Kemuning Kelas Jauh Sencalang, Riau. The study was motivated by limited classroom space, teaching personnel, and learning facilities, which required instruction to be organized into morning and afternoon shifts with different learning durations. A descriptive qualitative approach was employed. Data were collected through non-participant observation, in-depth interviews, and documentation involving five Social Studies teachers and supporting informants, including the principal, vice principal for curriculum, head of the main school, a school committee member, and students. Data were analyzed through data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification. The findings showed that teachers employed three main strategies: providing learning materials before face-to-face sessions, using Google Classroom to extend access to materials and assignments, and providing additional learning outside regular school hours. The teaching methods included lectures, discussions, and question-and-answer sessions, adjusted to subject characteristics and student conditions. Sociology and Geography teachers relied more heavily on discussion, whereas Economics, History, and Civic Education teachers more frequently combined lectures with question-and-answer sessions. From a Vygotskian social constructivist perspective, these strategies functioned as scaffolding that supported students within their Zone of Proximal Development. The study concluded that teachers’ adaptive capacity was important for maintaining learning effectiveness under the shift system.

Model for evaluating the effect of single-point diamond turning parameters on the diffraction efficiency and MTF of diffractive lenses
abstractText: We present a mathematical model relating single-point diamond turning machining parameters to the optical performance of diffractive lenses. The theoretical surface error is decomposed into a turning-groove structure and an ideal diffractive structure containing transmission blockages. Combining scalar diffraction theory with the phase-delay model, the effects of the tool nose radius and feed rate on the diffraction efficiency, polychromatic integral diffraction efficiency, and modulation transfer function are analyzed. A case study of a single-layer diffractive optical element for a 3.4- to 4.9-μm continuous-zoom system validates the model, providing a theoretical basis for selecting initial machining parameters and improving fabrication efficiency.

title: Polymer Assembly Mediated by Attractive Crowding Agents: Good-Solvent vs Poor-Solvent Polymers
abstractText: Abstract Polymer assembly dictates the functional performance of soft materials and is fundamentally associated with intracellular liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS), a ubiquitous process in living cells. Macromolecular crowding exerts dramatic regulatory effects on both assembly dynamics and condensate morphologies. Although extensive studies concerning macromolecular crowding effects have long focused on repulsive interactions, a systematic mechanistic picture describing how attractive crowders tune the structural and dynamic features of polymer assemblies and LLPS remains elusive. Herein, we construct a coarse-grained Langevin model to simulate polymer-crowder aggregation of good-solvent and poor-solvent chains by adjusting intercrowder attraction, crowder size and crowder concentration. Our results demonstrate a series of novel structural and kinetic features. Intercrowder interaction strength serves as a key switch governing condensate morphology: good-solvent polymers evolve sequentially from crowder-bridged clusters to homogeneous mixed droplets and core–shell assemblies, whereas poor-solvent chains form compact self-aggregates, cage-confined multiclusters or patchy core–shell structures. Crowders with large sizes impose dominant geometric packing restrictions, generating distinctive porous and layered condensates. Increasing crowder concentration can fully dissociate good-solvent polymer aggregates while merely breaking poor-solvent polymer clusters into small separated domains. Moreover, a prevailing three-step assembly mechanism involving nucleation, diffusion-limited lag and cluster coalescence is identified for all polymer systems. This work establishes an integrated framework interpreting the competition between crowding-mediated bridging and intrinsic assembly of poor-solvent polymers. The new insights yielded in this study enrich our understanding of intracellular condensates and provide useful guidance for functional polymer design.

abstractText: The rapid growth of digital technology and increased internet penetration in Indonesia present major opportunities in digital education. According to the Association of Indonesian Internet Service Providers (APJII), internet users in Indonesia reached 221.5 million in 2024, with most users aged 18–35 [1]. Despite projected annual growth of over 20% in the online education market, a gap remains between learning needs and users' purchasing power, as online course prices range from IDR 200,000 to IDR 2,000,000 per course. This study analyzes the business feasibility of SkillSwap, a digital learning platform using a teach-to-earn model where users earn learning credits by contributing knowledge rather than solely through payment. Market validation included a survey of 15 respondents (active students, fresh graduates, and self-learners), Business Model Canvas (BMC) analysis, competitor analysis, Figma-based wireframe design, and financial analysis (CapEx/OpEx, BEP, ROI). Survey results show 80% of respondents cite cost as the main barrier to online learning, and 93.4% have canceled course registrations due to financial constraints. Interest in the contribution-based model reached 73.3%. Financial analysis with an initial investment of IDR 18,950,000 indicates an operational Break-Even Point at month 11 with 13,000 Monthly Active Users (MAU) and a 6.9% ROI at the end of year two. These findings indicate that SkillSwap is feasible to develop as an inclusive and sustainable digital education platform.

Development and Evaluation of Andrographis paniculata Root Extract Cream: Effects of Stearic Acid and Triethanolamine on Stability and Antioxidant Activity
abstractText: Oxidative stress contributes to skin damage, highlighting the need for plant-derived topical antioxidants. This study aimed to evaluate antioxidant activity of Andrographis paniculata root extract and develop a stable antioxidant cream. Dried roots were macerated with 70% ethanol, and antioxidant activity was assessed using the DPPH scavenging assay with vitamin C as control. Three oil-in-water cream formulations containing 0.25% extract were prepared with different stearic acid and triethanolamine concentrations and evaluated after accelerated storage for organoleptic properties, pH, homogeneity, viscosity, spreadability, adhesion, emulsion type, and antioxidant activity. Extraction yielded 6.66% blackish-brown extract. The extract showed concentration-dependent antioxidant activity, with an IC50 of 16.55 ppm, while vitamin C showed activity with an IC50 of 4.72 ppm. All creams remained homogeneous, retained oil-in-water emulsion type, and showed no visible phase separation. Accelerated storage significantly increased pH in all formulations, significantly reduced viscosity only in Formula I, significantly increased spreadability only in Formula III, and did not significantly affect adhesion time. Higher stearic acid and triethanolamine concentrations increased viscosity and adhesion but reduced spreadability. The cream retained antioxidant activity, with an IC50 of 69.61 ppm. Overall, Formula II showed the most stable physical profile and is a promising candidate for herbal antioxidant development.

Analisis Kebutuhan Pengembangan E-LKM Berbasis Discovery Learning Terintegrasi Augmented Reality pada Materi Struktur Atom
abstractText: The development of digital teaching materials for chemistry instruction needs to consider learning conditions and student characteristics to align with needs in the field. This study aimed to analyze the need for developing E-LKM based on discovery learning and integrated with augmented reality (AR) for atomic structure. The study employed a descriptive approach, with preliminary data collected through structured interviews with three chemistry teachers and a needs analysis questionnaire completed by 111 students. Data were analyzed using descriptive percentages and qualitative descriptions of the teachers’ responses. The interview results showed that the teachers regarded atomic structure as a difficult topic. Assessment information referenced in the study indicated that 76.57% of students had not met the learning achievement criteria. The questionnaire results showed that 67% of students considered atomic structure moderately difficult and 17% considered it difficult. Instruction remained dominated by teacher explanations (54%), while textbooks were the most frequently used learning resource (57%). A total of 72% of students had difficulty visualizing the arrangement of protons, neutrons, and electrons, and 82% used mobile phones more frequently for social media than for learning. Nevertheless, 70% of students reported enjoying the use of technology to support learning, and 75% were interested or very interested in digital teaching materials accessible through mobile phones. These findings indicate a need for a structured E-LKM that guides students through the stages of discovery learning and provides three-dimensional visualizations through AR. This study provides a basis for designing digital teaching materials aligned with the needs of atomic structure instruction. However, the findings are limited to a preliminary needs analysis and do not yet provide evidence of the product’s validity or effectiveness.

title: Comparative evaluation of the effectiveness of NotebookLM-generated and delivered lectures for dental interns: an interventional study
abstractText: Abstract Background and objective The introduction of AI into the area of dental education provides a new opportunity through which to improve student learning outcomes. This study compared the effectiveness of traditional ‘live’ lectures with a video lecture produced and delivered by NotebookLM (Gemini Notebook) to teach endodontics to dental interns. Methods Two groups of dental interns were randomly assigned to receive either live lectures or NotebookLM videos on 3 progressively difficult endodontic subjects (diagnosis and treatment planning – basic; vital pulp therapy – intermediate; and root resorption – advanced). Both instructional delivery methods utilized identical source materials (current journal articles, books, and clinical practice guidelines). All students completed 15 multiple-choice questions designed to measure higher-level thinking skills, as well as self-assessment questionnaires measuring perceived learning outcomes and satisfaction after attending their respective training sessions. Results There were no significant differences in the diagnosis ( p = 0.327) or vital pulp therapy ( p = 0.411) post-test scenarios. However, the AI lecture group performed significantly better in the root resorption scenario (87.8% vs. 83.0%, p = 0.029). Students in the AI group reported significantly higher engagement on 2 items: the logical flow of the presentation ( p = 0.041) and the relevance of the topic to their training ( p = 0.024). A significant difference was also found for self-reported distraction ( p = 0.003), higher in the AI group (74.5% vs. 38.3%). The AI group was also favored in delivery style, content for note preparation, overall satisfaction, confidence on the topic after lecture, clinical application capability, clarification of complex concepts, and meeting of learning objectives (all p ≤ 0.012). For all other items in the questionnaire, there was no statistically significant difference between the groups. Conclusions NotebookLM-generated video lectures matched human-delivered lectures on immediate post-test performance for diagnosis and vital pulp therapy and yielded higher scores for root resorption, a difference that may be topic-specific. Interns also reported a favorable experience on the self-assessment questionnaire. Future research could examine the efficacy of student-AI educator interaction during interactive sessions, as well as long-term knowledge retention.

Educational Technologies Promote Treatment Adherence in Older People: A Scoping Review
abstractText: Abstract Purpose of Review The expansion of access to digital educational technologies among older adults with chronic noncommunicable diseases provides opportunities for their integration into primary health care practice. Although evidence-based tools are essential for fostering self-care, clinicians must still identify where these tools fit into daily practice. This scoping review mapped educational health technologies designed to improve therapeutic adherence among older adults with chronic noncommunicable diseases in Primary Health Care and community settings, following the Joanna Briggs Institute guidelines. The search strategy covered the Nursing Database (BDENF), Latin American and Caribbean Health Sciences Literature (LILACS), Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Scopus, Web of Science, and MEDLINE from 2024 to December 2025. Recent Findings Technologies that support treatment adherence in older adults can improve care by optimizing clinical self-management and fostering health literacy. Self-management tools compensate for prospective memory deficits and manage complex chronic regimens through alarms, glycemic monitoring, and structured support, whereas health literacy tools reduce cognitive and communication barriers. By using audiovisual resources, universal symbols, and intuitive interfaces, these technologies clarify prescriptions, facilitate deprescribing, and strengthen patients’ active engagement in shared decision-making. Summary The technologies reviewed support cognitive and informational self-management, which may thereby strengthen medication adherence. By reducing the cognitive load of treatment management, these resources may foster autonomy among older adults and ease the difficulties of managing complex regimens.

title: Exploring the Proton Conductivity across the C-Dots Doped Cellulose Nanocrystal Biopolymer
abstractText: Abstract Biopolymers have gained significant attention across the energy, fuel, bioelectronics, and biomedical applications owing to their intrinsic protonic conductivity. Among them, polysaccharides represent a class of low-cost and abundant biomacromolecules suitable for constructing functional biopolymers. In this work, we present a novel strategy to enhance proton conduction in biopolymer systems by integrating varying concentrations of carbon dot (C-Dot)-derived surface functional groups into a cellulose nanocrystal (CNC) biopolymer. Blue-, green-, and red-emitting C-Dots, with varying degrees of oxygen-rich surface functional groups and heterocyclic nitrogen-enriched core states, were incorporated as dopants into the CNC biopolymer. Notably, the inclusion of B-, G-, and R-C-Dots led to ∼2-, 4-, and 10-fold enhancements in protonic conductivity, respectively, compared to pristine CNC biopolymer. This approach provides an effective pathway for designing advanced self-assembled biopolymer proton-conducting materials for next-generation bioprotonic applications.

title: Developmental Changes in Symptoms and Adaptive Functioning in Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Real-World Longitudinal Perspective
abstractText: Objective To evaluate longitudinal changes in adaptive functioning measured by the Korean Vineland Adaptive Behavior Scales, Second Edition (K-VABS-II) in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) receiving routine outpatient care.Methods This retrospective study analyzed data from 156 children (aged 2–7 years) who completed at least two K-VABS-II assessments at a tertiary university hospital. Additional evaluations included the Korean version of the Childhood Autism Rating Scale, Second Edition- Standard Version (K-CARS2-ST) and the Beery–Buktenica Developmental Test of Visual–Motor Integration, Sixth Edition (VMI-6).Results The K-VABS-II Adaptive Behavior Composite score declined significantly from a baseline of 56.07 to 54.10 (p<0.05) over an average interval of 24.14 months. Daily living skills and socialization showed the most pronounced reductions (p<0.001), while communication and motor skills remained stable. VMI-6 scores also declined significantly (p<0.05), while K-CARS2-ST scores showed no meaningful change (p=0.859).Conclusion Longitudinal evaluations using the K-VABS-II revealed significant declines in adaptive functioning among children with ASD, even when core symptom severity remained stable. These findings highlight that functional development may follow a divergent path from symptom trajectories and remain vulnerable to regression without adequate support. This underscores the critical need for early and sustained interventions to promote adaptive outcomes and the urgent development of innovative pediatric therapeutics.Trial Registration: Clinical Research Information Service Identifier: KCT0010881

title: Knowledge, attitude, and perception of cardiac and pulmonary telerehabilitation among physiotherapists in India
abstractText: Abstract Despite well-established and tangible effects of cardiopulmonary rehabilitation, patient uptake is lower in middle-and-low-income countries. Telerehabilitation provides an opportunity to reduce barriers, improve access and program adherence. In India, as the cardiopulmonary telerehabilitation model is comparatively new, it is important to assess knowledge, attitude, and perception among physiotherapists. A cross-sectional study was conducted among Indian physiotherapists via a validated 29-item questionnaire. Questions focused on demographics, work experience, educational qualification, Knowledge, Attitude, and Perception of telerehabilitation. 121 physiotherapists participated in the study; most of them were MPT-qualified, with 2–7 years of experience. Overall, 72.7% demonstrated essential understanding to implement a cardiopulmonary TR program, while only 34.7% were aware of standardised protocols. 56.2% believed they could implement it safely and effectively, and 63.6% were willing to include it in regular practice. 95.9% believed this model could make significant differences in the quality of life of patients, and 78.5% felt it to be as effective as centre-based rehabilitation program. 99.2% felt the need for training before implementation. Findings show that even though there is good amount of awareness, attitude, and positive perception regarding telerehabilitation among physiotherapists, its training and actual application in routine practice is still lacking.

Impact of Significant Others on Antenatal Care Utilization among Ever-Married Women in Nigeria: A Cross-Sectional Study
abstractText: Abstract Objective Reproductive health decisions are rarely made solely by women; beyond individual and sociodemographic characteristics, significant others such as spouses, mothers, mothers-in-law, and community play important roles in women’s Antenatal Care (ANC) seeking behaviours. Therefore, this paper examines the significant others’ impact and their associations with ANC utilization among Ever-Married Nigerian Women who have ever been pregnant or are currently pregnant. Method A cross-sectional design using stratified multi-stage sampling with probability proportional to size was conducted among women of reproductive age (15 − 49 years) in Nigeria. The impact of significant others on ANC adequacy among 1,328 women who have past/currently pregnancy was examined. The data collected were analysed at three levels: univariate, bivariate, and multivariable analyses using a multinomial logistic regression model. Results The results revealed that 39.4% of the women who received adequate ANC experienced a positive significant others’ impact, as against 25.5% who experienced a negative significant others’ impact. Adequacy of ANC was significantly associated with significant others’ impact, employment status, and wanting pregnancy at the time among women. Women who have a positive significant other’s impact were significantly twice as likely (AOR = 2.190; 95% C.I. = 1.244–3.855; p = 0.007) to receive adequate ANC compared to those who have a negative impact. Conclusion This study found a significant association between ANC adequacy and significant others’ impact during pregnancy in the study area. Overall, the inadequacy of ANC in this study reflects a composite interaction of geographic and psychosocial factors, consistent with national evidence that ANC utilisation in Nigeria remains persistent and unevenly distributed across regions and social groups. Therefore, targeted interventions are necessary to promote employment opportunities, financial autonomy, pregnancy planning, reproductive health education, women’s autonomy, and a supportive household environment, thereby enhancing ANC adequacy and improving maternal health outcomes.

Cognitive impairment, medial temporal lobe changes, and fluid biomarkers of Alzheimer’s disease and neurodegeneration following herpes simplex virus type 1 encephalitis
abstractText: Abstract Background Herpesvirus encephalitis is a severe brain infection, in adults most often caused by herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1). It predominantly affects the medial temporal lobes (MTL), which are critical for memory functions. Links have been discussed between herpes virus infections and Alzheimer’s disease (AD). We therefore investigated cognitive function, structural brain changes, and fluid biomarkers related to AD and other neurodegenerative processes in individuals with previous herpes simplex virus type 1 encephalitis (HSE). Methods Eleven patients with prior HSE were retrospectively identified using a clinical CSF laboratory database. Control groups included 44 cognitively unimpaired (CU) individuals, 44 mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and 22 AD dementia patients from the Swedish BioFINDER-2 study. Groups were stratified by amyloid-β (Aβ) status using CSF Aβ42/Aβ40. All participants underwent neuropsychological testing. Structural brain changes were assessed using 7T or 3T MRI including visual evaluation of lesions and automated segmentation of MTL subregions. Plasma biomarkers (tau phosphorylated at position 217 (p-tau217), p-tau181, glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), and neurofilament light (NfL)) were measured using immunoassays. Results The mean follow-up time since infection was 6.5 years. The encephalitis group (mean age 49 years, 55% females) was age-matched to the CU Aβ- group but younger than other groups. MRI findings in the encephalitis group ranged from marked unilateral MTL atrophy to no visible changes. Compared with CU individuals, encephalitis patients showed significantly impaired episodic memory (delayed recall) and lower global cognition, comparable to MCI but less severe than AD dementia. Within the encephalitis group, episodic memory impairment was associated with visually assessed MTL atrophy ( p = 0.0185). In hemispheres without gross atrophy, MTL subregional volumes resembled CU and MCI but were larger than in AD dementia. Plasma p-tau217 and GFAP levels were elevated in the full HSE-group compared with Aβ-negative CU and MCI, but lower than in AD dementia. P-tau181 and NfL levels were similar to CU. P-tau217 was not significantly different between Aβ-negative HSE and Aβ-negative CU. Associations between GFAP and cognitive performance were no longer significant after exclusion of the two patients with Fazekas grade 3 white matter lesions. Conclusions Previous HSE was associated with substantial heterogeneity in long-term cognitive performance, with poorer delayed recall associated with longer time since infection. Cognitive findings were also related to focal MTL atrophy, supporting a contribution of structural injury to long-term cognitive outcomes. Only a minority of the patients had signs of AD pathology by CSF biomarkers. Larger longitudinal studies are needed to determine the trajectories and mechanisms of cognitive change following HSE.

abstractText: Remaja pesantren menghadapi tuntutan akademik dan keagamaan yang padat sehingga berisiko mengalami stres akademik. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis hubungan manajemen waktu dan kondisi fisik dengan stres akademik pada santriwati. Penelitian kuantitatif dengan desain cross-sectional ini dilakukan pada santriwati sebuah pesantren di Kabupaten Aceh Besar. Sebanyak 189 dari 360 santriwati dipilih dengan purposive sampling. Data dikumpulkan dengan Time Management Behavior Scale, Physical Health Questionnaire, dan Educational Stress Scale for Adolescents, lalu dianalisis dengan uji chi-square dan regresi logistik ordinal. Sebagian besar responden mengalami stres akademik sedang (72,0%). Secara bivariat, kondisi fisik (χ²=36,172; p<0,001) dan manajemen waktu (χ²=75,025; p<0,001) berhubungan dengan stres akademik. Dalam analisis multivariat, kondisi fisik (B=−0,809; p=0,001) dan manajemen waktu (B=−1,185; p<0,001) tetap berhubungan negatif dengan stres akademik. Nilai Nagelkerke R² sebesar 0,207 menunjukkan bahwa model menjelaskan sekitar 20,7% variasi tingkat stres akademik. Manajemen waktu dan kondisi fisik yang lebih baik berasosiasi dengan peluang stres akademik tinggi yang lebih kecil, sehingga keduanya layak menjadi sasaran program pendampingan santri.

title: DARI PENDAMPINGAN MENUJU KEMANDIRIAN: PENGUATAN KELEMBAGAAN BUM DESA “ARGO MAJU SEJAHTERA” MELALUI PENGABDIAN MASYARAKAT BERBASIS ASET
abstractText: Village-Owned Enterprises (BUMDes) frequently confront institutional capacity deficits despite possessing abundant rural endowments. This community service project documents the institutional strengthening of BUMDes "Argo Maju Sejahtera" in Argoyuwono Village, Ampelgading District, Malang Regency. The partner's foundational problem stemmed from three dormant business pilots and unmanaged manure generated by 15,240 goats across the village. The intervention applied the Asset-Based Community Development (ABCD) framework operationalized across five cyclical phases (discovery, dream, design, define, and destiny). Participatory methods engaged 28 key stakeholders representing the village administration, BUMDes executives, and local livestock farmer groups through four Focus Group Discussions (FGD) and business simulation clinics. Tangible outputs comprised a validated feasibility study for a goat-manure organic fertilizer unit projecting an operating profit of IDR 5,000,000 per production cycle, formalized organizational job allocations, and ratified Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) governing operational and financial controls. This initiative demonstrates that an asset-based paradigm successfully shifts community mindsets from external dependency to internal resource valorization. ABSTRAK Badan Usaha Milik Desa (BUM Desa) kerap menghadapi persoalan klasik berupa melimpahnya potensi sumber daya alam yang belum diimbangi kapasitas kelembagaan memadai. title: Air pollution is associated with a distinct pathogen spectrum in community-acquired pneumonia: a prospective multicentre cohort study
abstractText: Abstract Background Community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) is the leading cause of death due to infection worldwide, with its incidence and disease course influenced by air pollution exposure. Little is known about how air pollution influences microbiological findings in patients with CAP. Methods Patients were recruited from a prospective, multicentre study of CAP (CAPNETZ). Air pollution data were collected at the city level considering data up to one month before inclusion. Associations with sputum pathogen detection and cell counts were tested using generalised linear mixed-effects logistic regression models adjusting for clinical confounders, centre-level heterogeneity and meteorological data. Internal validation was performed using an Ensemble Feature Selection (EFS) approach. Results Among 4,446 eligible patients with available sputum samples, a potential pathogen was detected in 1,581 patients, while complete sputum-cell-count data were available for 4,014 patients. Detection of Streptococcus pneumoniae was associated with previous higher exposure to sulphur dioxide (SO 2 ) (OR 1.75, p = 0.008) and carbon monoxide (CO) (OR 1.57, p = 0.02). Escherichia coli was more frequently detected in patients who were exposed to elevated levels of nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ) (OR 2.75, p = 0.004) and higher temperature (OR 1.51, p = 0.03), whereas increased fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) exposure (OR 0.37, p = 0.001) was linked to reduced detection. Furthermore, SO 2 exposure influenced the likelihood of obtaining a diagnostically relevant sputum culture and was associated with higher odds of detecting a high leucocyte count (OR 1.18, p = 0.02). Results were largely corroborated by EFS, particularly for S. pneumoniae and E. coli detection. Conclusion Exposure to air pollution was associated with a distinct pathogen spectrum in patients with CAP. These findings may have implications for the interpretation of microbiological data in an epidemiological and clinical context and highlight the importance of considering air pollution exposure as a confounding factor. Further validation in cohorts with high-quality environmental, microbiological and antimicrobial resistance data is needed. Peers reaching peers: a case study on expanding contraceptive access for female sex workers in Uganda
abstractText: Background Female sex workers (FSWs) face disproportionately high rates of unintended pregnancy and unmet family planning needs. Peer-led interventions offer a promising strategy to expand access to contraceptives for populations such as FSWs that are routinely stigmatized or otherwise left behind by traditional healthcare facilities. Methods We trained 50 peer educators across four divisions of Nansana Municipality in Uganda to deliver contraceptive education and provide free short-acting contraceptives directly to FSWs. Peer educators also facilitated referrals as needed to a stigma-free clinic offering long-term contraceptives, and comprehensive sexual and reproductive health services. Peer educators were trained in destigmatizing sexual and reproductive health service provision for FSWs specifically. Providing these services at a designated clinic minimized structural barriers, such as stock-outs and disrespectful provider attitudes, enabling effective referrals and service uptake. Results Over 12 months, 787 FSWs received contraceptive education: 5420 male and 510 female condoms were distributed, 232 FSWs accepted oral contraceptives, and 179 were referred for and received long-acting methods, with 74 receiving injectables and 105 implants or intrauterine devices. Conclusions Peer-led models can expand contraceptive access among FSWs in designated stigma-free facilities with reliable supply chains. To achieve sustainable contraceptive access among FSWs more broadly, this approach should be integrated into government sexual and reproductive health systems.

abstractText: The utilization of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI), specifically ChatGPT, holds strong potential for accelerating the design of instructional materials in schools. This qualitative descriptive study aims to describe the implementation of ChatGPT training for teachers at SMP Negeri 40 Samarinda, identify the technical challenges encountered, and analyze changes in participants' understanding when drafting teaching modules and Student Worksheets (LKPD). The training involved 24 teachers, from whom five participants were purposively selected as in-depth interview informants based on subject diversity and active workshop participation. Data were gathered through observational procedures, artifact analysis of generated instructional designs, and post-training interviews analyzed thematically. The findings indicate that the training offered structured experiences for participants in formulating prompts based on Learning Outcomes (Capaian Pembelajaran) and Learning Objectives (Tujuan Pembelajaran). The primary challenges identified centered on fine-tuning prompt precision, limited simulation time, and presentation screen visibility. Based on artifact comparisons between initial and revised drafts, participants demonstrated critical evaluation skills by correcting contextual discrepancies in ChatGPT outputs before classroom integration. ABSTRAK Pemanfaatan Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI), khususnya ChatGPT, berpotensi mempercepat penyusunan perangkat pembelajaran di sekolah. Penelitian deskriptif kualitatif ini bertujuan untuk mendeskripsikan pelaksanaan pelatihan ChatGPT bagi guru di SMP Negeri 40 Samarinda, mengidentifikasi kendala teknis yang dihadapi, serta menganalisis perubahan pemahaman peserta dalam menyusun modul ajar dan Lembar Kerja Peserta Didik (LKPD). Pelatihan ini diikuti oleh 24 guru, dengan 5 peserta dipilih secara bertujuan (purposive) sebagai informan wawancara mendalam berdasarkan variasi mata pelajaran dan keaktifan praktik. Data dikumpulkan melalui observasi proses, analisis dokumen rancangan pembelajaran, serta wawancara pascapraktik yang dianalisis secara tematik. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa pelatihan memberikan pengalaman terarah bagi peserta dalam merumuskan instruksi (prompt) berbasis Capaian Pembelajaran (CP) dan Tujuan Pembelajaran (TP). Kendala utama yang teridentifikasi berpusat pada penyesuaian instruksi yang presisi, alokasi waktu simulasi yang terbatas, serta visibilitas media presentasi. Berdasarkan perbandingan draf awal dan akhir, peserta mulai menunjukkan kemampuan evaluasi kritis dengan menyunting kekeliruan kontekstual keluaran ChatGPT sebelum diintegrasikan ke dalam kelas.

Implementasi Algoritma Insertion Sort dan Interpolation Search dalam Penentuan Member Berprestasi Di Asrama Bahasa
abstractText: Managing student grade data at the Language Dormitory requires a system capable of performing ranking and data retrieval quickly and accurately. The current manual process has the potential to cause delays and errors in compiling rankings. This study aims to implement the Insertion Sort and Interpolation Search algorithms in the student grade management system. Specifically conducted at the Central Language Dormitory of Pondok Pesantren Salafiyah Syafi’iyah Sukorejo, this study integrates data such as student IDs, names, and average scores into an array data structure. Insertion Sort is utilized to sort the average exam scores from highest to lowest, while Interpolation Search is leveraged to accelerate the data retrieval process based on the searched score. Testing was conducted using 70 student grade records to evaluate the performance of both algorithms. The results indicate that Insertion Sort is capable of consistently producing sorted grades without requiring significant additional storage space, thanks to its stable and in-place processing characteristics. Meanwhile, Interpolation Search can locate data rapidly when applied to datasets with a relatively even distribution of values. Through its position calculation formula, this search algorithm proved to be highly efficient with an average time complexity of , where in the tracking experiment for the highest score of 88.70, the data was successfully found instantly in just 1 iteration. The implementation of both algorithms helps improve the efficiency of academic data management, speeds up the ranking and retrieval processes, and reduces the likelihood of errors in processing student grade data.

title: The Relationship between Need for Cognition and Chemistry Learning Interest among Senior High School Students: A Chain Mediation Model of Chemistry Self-Efficacy and Self-Regulation
abstractText: Abstract Chemistry learning interest plays a crucial role in sustaining students’ engagement with chemistry and supporting their long-term development in science learning. Need for cognition is regarded as an important intellectual investment trait that may be associated with students’ willingness to engage in effortful thinking and complex problem solving. Although previous studies have provided evidence for the association between need for cognition and academic interest, the psychological mechanisms underlying this relationship in the context of chemistry education remain insufficiently examined. Therefore, this study aims to investigate the multiple mediating pathways involving chemistry self-efficacy and self-regulation in the relationship between need for cognition and chemistry learning interest. A multiple-mediation model was constructed by drawing on intellectual investment theory and social cognitive theory, with Social Cognitive Career Theory specifically informing the self-efficacy–interest pathway and research on interest development informing the conceptualization of interest. Data were collected from grade 10 students in China (N = 3,431) using scales to measure need for cognition, chemistry learning interest, chemistry self-efficacy, and self-regulation. The results indicated that (1) need for cognition was significantly and positively associated with students’ chemistry learning interest; (2) chemistry self-efficacy showed a significant indirect effect in the association between need for cognition and chemistry learning interest; (3) self-regulation also showed a significant indirect effect in this association; and (4) need for cognition was indirectly associated with chemistry learning interest through a sequential mediation path involving chemistry self-efficacy and self-regulation. This study provides evidence for a theoretically plausible pattern of associations linking need for cognition to chemistry learning interest through capability beliefs and learning-regulation processes, contributing to a more integrated understanding of the relationship between students’ cognitive-motivational dispositions and domain-specific interest.Finally, the study provides pedagogical implications for supporting students’ chemistry learning interest by attending to cognitive engagement, chemistry self-efficacy, and self-regulated learning.

title: IMPLEMENTATION READINESS OF INTEGRATED COMMUNAL WASTEWATER AND FAECAL SLUDGE TREATMENT
abstractText: Decentralized wastewater treatment systems, which predominate in settlement areas, face challenges in the periodic management of faecal sludge due to limited access to centralized faecal sludge treatment facilities. This study assessed the implementation readiness of communal wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) integrated with on-site faecal sludge treatment system (SIPALT) in settlement areas within the Citarum Watershed. Wastewater quality was analyzed at 15 communal WWTPs using the Wastewater Quality Index (WWQI), which showed that effluent quality was categorized as moderately to slightly polluted. Faecal sludge from most communal WWTPs indicated low organic pollution according to the Organic Pollution Index (OPI) but high contamination according to the Contamination Index (CI). The performance of most communal WWTPs, assessed using the Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) method, yielded scores above 40%, indicating potential for improvement through SIPALT implementation. Cluster analysis (CA) and multiple discriminant analysis (MDA) were used to prioritize SIPALT technologies and classify implementation readiness into three categories based on technical, environmental, and community-related factors. Communal WWTPs categorized as less ready or not ready for SIPALT implementation require improvements, particularly in effluent quality, water supply, faecal sludge quality, land use, community perceptions, and community participation.
